caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 333 of 2005
lawyer:
Asad Hossain Choudhury, Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners.
Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos. 1-3 
Respondent Nos.4-9 ------ Not represented.
parties:
Abdul Khaleque Pramanik being dead his legal representatives; Mossammat Chandrabhan Bewa and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Rajab Ali Pramanik and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 28.11.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2341 of 1996)
full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J.: Mossammat Mobitan Bewa and her son Md. Mojibar Rahman Pramanik being substituted in place of their predecessor defendant Abdul Khaleque along with heirs of deceased defendant Abu Sayed Pramanik and three other defendants have preferred this petition for leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 28.11.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2341 of 1996 making the rule absolute.

2. The facts, in short, are that the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 to 4 instituted Other Suit No.19 of 1986 which was renumbered as Other Suit No.134 of 1990 for declaration of their title in the suit land stating, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to landlord Amatullah Gasu and others and one Ali Mamud was a Korfa Tenant under them and accordingly C.S Khatian No.441 of Mouza Rahabol was published and that Ali Mamud died leaving one son named Hurmat Ali and a widow named Khushiban Bibi, the plaintiff No. 5; thereafter Hurmat Ali died leaving three sons plaintiff Nos. 1 to 3 and a daughter plaintiff No.4 and they have been possessing the suit had peacefully for more than 12 years by cultivating and growing crops; that under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the plaintiffs acquired riot right in the suit land under the Government and that the defendant disclosed that M.R.R. Khatian for the suit land has been prepared in their names though they have no right, title and possession in the suit land and that the defendants asked the plaintiff to give up possession of the suit land in their favour and that the plaintiffs thereafter searched the Revenue Office and then came to know that M.R.R. Khatian has been prepared in the names of the defendants and as such to remove cloud in their title the plaintiffs instituted the suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 to 5 filed written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and stated that the suit land originally belonged to Khedmot Ullah predecessor of the defendants who died leaving wife Masiran and two sons Ajmatullah and Tajmatullah and that I Masiran died leaving her aforesaid two sons and that the predecessor of the plaintiffs Ali Mamud was a Korf tenant under Ajmatullah and others and that Ali Mamud failed to pay rent and so surrendered his Korfa tenancy right in favour of the landlord Ajmatullah and others and Ajmatullah died leaving three sons i.e. defendant Nos. 1 to 3 and a granddaughter Laity through her deceased daughter Anisar and that Ajmatullah transferred his share to Ataul Hoque and others and the predecessors of the defendants paid rent to the landlord and thereafter to the Government and M.R.R. Khatian No. 475 has been correctly prepared in the names of Ajmatullah, Tajmatullah, Masiran Bewa and Abdul Gafur and that the defendant No.2 set up a pump for irrigation in the suit land and in the month of Agrahayan, 1395 B.S. the plaintiffs took away the water pump for which the defendants filed a case against them.

<u>4. It has further been averred by the defendants that the plaintiffs suppressed the summons of the suit i.e. Other Suit No.19 of 1986, obtained an ex-parte decree whereupon the defendant filed Miscellaneous Case No.20 of 1987 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was allowed and that during pendency of the said Miscellaneous Case the plaintiff constructed illegally a house in the suit land and that there is no merit in the suit of the plaintiff and as such it is liable to be dismissed.</u>

5. The trial court recorded evidence of witnesses produced by both the parties and by judgment and decree dated 26.10.1994 dismissed the suit.

6. The plaintiff respondents preferred Other Appeal No.282 of 1994 which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Bogra and the aforesaid lower appellate court by the judgment and decree dated 23.05.1996 dismissed the appeal thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court.

7. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs moved the High Court Division under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in Civil Revision No.2341 of 1996 which was heard by a teamed Single Judge who by impugned judgment and order made the rule absolute, setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the courts below and thus decreed the suit.

8. Hence is this petition.

9. In support of the petition Mr. Asad Hossain Choudhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners has taken us through the impugned judgment and other materials.

10. He submits that the plaintiffs had failed to prove their case up to the hilt since they had no rent-receipts and initially plaint was silent as to the possession through erection of huts and by their subsequent amendment, they made out a new case. The trial court had grounded his judgment on the basis of evidence meticulously canvassed. And the appellate court taking up all the points had confirmed by a plausible reasoning the trial court's judgment

11. He then submits that the defendants had proved their case by submitting their documentary evidence such as Modified Rent-Roll, series of rent-receipts, Mutation khatian etc.  only that Ali Mamud possessed the suit I land for 3 years thereafter his sons did not possess the same but this statement has I not been corroborated by any other witness. The statements of the D.Ws. also do not speak of surrendering possession of the suit land in favour of the original land-lord."

12. Lastly he submits that the onus is upon the plaintiffs to prove their case independently and not upon the weakness of the defendants.

13. We have considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate and' perused materials on record.

14. The basis of the claim of the defendant petitioners is the story of surrender purported to have been made by Ali Mamud. The High Court Division in this connection appears to have considered the facts and circumstances and evidence on record and observed: "I have gone through the evidences on record and found that D.W. 1 stated that he did not see Ali Mamud to surrender possession and he has no paper to show that Ali Mamud ever surrendered possession and he also failed to mention the date of surrender. D.W. 1 M. Fazlul Huq claimed to be the successor of the original landlord and he alleged to have purchased 1 some lands from the com-sharer of the suit land. He is aged about 50 years and as such he is not a competent person to say or explain about the surrender. D.W.2 though is a man of 76 years old but he has stated

15. The High Court Division further observed:-

"The C.S. record shows that Ali Mamud predecessor of the plaintiffs hid Korf a tenancy in the suit land and possession of All Mamud in the suit land was uninterrupted and on the commencement' of the Bangal Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1928 he had become a occupancy raiyat and then settled raiyat under Sections 19 and 20 of the Bengal Tenancy Act."

16. Regarding possession of the parties the High Court Division found:

"The plaintiffs have succeeded in proving that they have continuous possession in the suit land since the time of Ali Mahmud and after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force, the petitioners as heirs of Ali Mahmud has become tenant by operation of law under the government."

<u>17. In view of the materials on record we hold that as M.R.R. Khatian appears to have been recorded in the names of the defendants they could pay rents in respect of the suit land for some period and mutated their names but the defendants failed to prove that the predecessor of the plaintiffs surrendered possession of the suit land and the defendants admitted possession of the plaintiffs. The basis of the claim of the defendant is surrender of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. In the absence of any evidence as to surrender allegedly made by the predecessor of the plaintiffs we are of the view that the preparation of M.R.R. record in the name of the defendants cannot stand in the claim of the plaintiff and as such the High Court Division considering the facts and circumstances and evidence on record reversed the finding of the courts below and thus made the rule absolute.</u>

18. We have perused the impugned Judgment and order of the High Court Division and in the facts and circumstance of the case we are of the view that the High Court Division correctly decided the case. The impugned judgment therefore does not call for interference.

19. In view of the discussion made above, the petition appears to be without any merit.

20. The petition is accordingly dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1968 of 2009
lawyer:
Probir Neogi, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Harun-or-Rashid, Advocate instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Millon Nayeb ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Joynal Abedin Mia and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 06.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2707 of 2003)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: This Civil Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and order dated 06.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2707 of 2003 making the rule absolute.

2. The short facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this civil petition for leave to appeal are that the present petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No.68 of 1997 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal praying for setting aside the preliminary and final decree dated 31.03.1988 and 16.06.1997 respectively passed in Partition Suit No. 89 of 1984 of that court on the ground of non-service of summon.

3. The opposite party No. 7 contested in that miscellaneous case by filing written objection. The material case of this contesting opposite party was that the partition suit was originally filed in the year 1968 and it was then numbered as Title Suit No. 203 of 1968 and subsequently on transfer it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 89 of 1984. That summons of that suit was duly served upon all the defendants including the petitioner; that some of the defendants who were close relations of the petitioner, contested that suit; that the petitioner being a close relation of the contesting defendants was fully aware of that suit and the decree passed therein. The further case of this contesting opposite party was that another defendant, namely, the defendant No.13 of that partition suit also filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 21 of 1990 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the decree passed in that partition suit and that miscellaneous case was ultimately dismissed on contest; that the present petitioner knowing about all these facts filed the present miscellaneous case on false pleas.

<u>4. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence and facts and circumstances, dismissed the miscellaneous case filed by this petitioner. This petitioner then preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 63 of 2001 in the court of the District Judge, Barisal against that judgment of the trial court. The said appeal was ultimately heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Barisal who allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment and order of the trail court. The contesting opposite party No. 7 preferred Civil Revision No. 2707 of 2003 calling in question the said judgment and order of the appellate court below and obtained rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing, made that rule absolute setting aside the judgment and order of the appellate court below and restoring those of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order.</u>

5. Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned advocate has appeared for the petitioner while Mr. Harun-or-Rashid, the learned advocate has appeared for the respondents.

6. We have heard the learned advocates of both the sides.

<u>7. Mr. Probir Neogi has made submission to the effect that in this miscellaneous case the opposite party could not prove at all that the summons of the original partition suit was served upon this petitioner and in the circumstances the trial court has committed illegality in rejecting the miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by this petitioner and the High Court Division also has committed error in affirming this judgment and order of the trial court.</u>

8. Mr. Harun-or-Rashid, on the other hand, has made submission to the effect that the original partition suit was filed long 41 years before and that some very close relations Of this petitioner contested that partition suit and in the circumstances it is not believable and acceptable at all that this petitioner did not know about that partition suit and the decree passed therein.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and also the judgments of the appellate court below and of the trial court.

<u>10. It appears that the trial court, on examination of record of the partition suit in question and considering the evidence and the facts and circumstances found that the summons of the original suit was duly served upon the predecessor of the petitioner and after his death upon the petitioner also and that the petitioner had knowledge about the suit and the decree passed therein. The High Court Division upon consideration of facts and circumstances on record has affirmed this finding of the trial court. We do not find any wrong or illegality in this concurrent findings of the trial court and the High Court Division.</u>

<u>11. In a case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioner is to prove also that he has filed the case within the statutory period of limitation. In the present case the petitioner could not prove this fact; rather there are ample facts and circumstances on record which tell that the petitioner filed this case long after the statutory period of limitation from the date of his knowledge about the decree in question.</u>

12. In the circumstances we find no merit in this civil petition for leave to appeal and hence it is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Review Petition No. 146 of 2008
lawyer:
Abdus Salam Khan, Advocate, instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiya, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
Not represented ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
M.A. Aziz.  ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Bangladesh Secretariat, Ramna, Dhaka and another.  ------ Respondents.
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 19.06.2008 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil appeal No. 181 of 2005.)
full_judgment:
Md. Joynul Abedin J: <u>By this petition the defendant-petitioner seeks review of this Court's judgment dated 19.06.2008 passed in Civil Appeal No. 181 of 2005 dismissing the appeal with cost of Tk. 10,000/-</u>

<u>2. Short fact of the case is that the respondent No. 1 as the plaintiff filed the Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 in the Court of The Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka alleging, inter-alia, that decree passed on 14.08.1972 in Title Suit No. 64 of the Court of First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka was obtained by practising fraud and forgery upon the Court by the defendant No. 1 and as such the same is void and not binding on the Government for a declaration that the judgment dated 10.04.1997 passed in Writ Petition No. 2456 of 1996 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 744 of 1997 on the basis of the aforesaid decree in Title Suit No. 64 of 1972 were also obtained by practising fraud and forgery on the Court and are therefore inoperative, null and void and have no legal force and as such not binding upon the plaintiff and for a further declaration that the schedule No. 1 property was not the subject matter of the solenama decree in the Title Suit No. 64 of 1972 a decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendant No. 1 from claiming or demanding or interfering with and /or disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in schedule No,  property and to award cost of the suit and to pass such other and further order or orders as court may deem fit and proper as per law and equity.</u>

3. The plaintiff-respondent considering the facts and circumstances of the case filed a petition for transfer of the suit to High Court Division under Article 110 of the Constitution. Accordingly the said suit was transferred to a Division Bench of the High Court Division comprising Mr. Justice Kazi A. T. Monawaruddin and Mr. Justice Md. Muzammel Hossain and a rule was issued in Transfer petition No. 2 of 2000 which is still pending.

<u>4. Defendant No. 1 appeared in the Transfer Petition No. 2 of 2000 and filed an application for discharging the Rule stating, inter-alia, that the Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 was fixed on 11.09.2002 for steps of the plaintiff but the plaintiff failed to take necessary steps whereupon the Joint District Judge fixed 14.11.2002 for steps of the plaintiff and on that date the plaintiff filed an application for adjournment to take steps. Thereafter, the plaintiff again failed to take necessary steps on the fixed dates and the suit was dismissed for default on 22.04.2003. The plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 filed and application on 27.10.2003 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the trial. Court for restoration of the said Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 and upon hearing the plaintiff-petitioner, the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka rejected the application for restoration by his order No. 15 dated 06.11.2003. Thereafter, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 2003 under order 9 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 11.11.2003 for restoration of the aforesaid title suit, which is still pending in the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and the Miscellaneous Case was fixed on 20.01.2004 for filing written objection by the respondent No. 1. The respondent No.1 filled an application for calling for the record of Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 by suppressing the fact that the suit was not pending in the lower Court, upon hearing the learned Advocate of the respondent the Bench consisting of Mr. Justice Amirul kabir Chowdhury and Mr. Justice Syed A. B. Mahmudul Haque were pleased to call for the record though there was no such suit pending in the lower Court. Actually when the title suit was dismissed for default on 22.04.2003 the present rule automatically became infructuous. The respondent filed this transfer petition for withdrawal of Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 which was pending in the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and during pendency of the present rule the title suit was dis-missed for default on 22.04.2003 and the Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 2003 for restoration is still pending and as such the present rule has become infractuous as it is the mandatory provision of Article 110 of the Constitution that a suit must be pending in the lower Court which is to be withdrawn. Since Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 is not pending in the Court of 3rd Joint District Judge, Dhaka there is no question of withdrawal of that suit for disposal by the High Court Division and as such the instant rule became infractuous.</u>

5. Thereafter, the plaintiff-respondent filed an application for hearing of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 2003 arising out of Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 now pending in the Court of 3rd Joint Distract Judge, Dhaka. The High Court Division thereafter allowed the petition for hearing of the Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 2003 and fixed the matter for hearing.

6. 13eing aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and order the defendant petitioner moved the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No. 181 of 2005. After hearing the Appellate Division dismissed the appeal.

7. In this backdrop, the petitioner filed this civil review petition.

8. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that it is an error apparent on the face of the judgment of the Appellate Division in that the Appellate Division manifestly failed to consider that the Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 2003 for restoration of Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 to its original file and number by setting aside the dismissal order dated 22.04.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka is not a case as contemplated under Article 110 of the Constitution for disposal by the High Court Division and therefore, the High court Division acted without jurisdiction in allowing the hearing of the above Miscellaneous Case by itself which is not contemplated under Article 110 of the Constitution. He further submits that it is an error apparent on the face of the judgment of the Appellate Division that the said Division glaringly omitted to take notice of the fact that the Miscellaneous Case No. 88 of 2003 was filed under order IX, Rule IV of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of Title Suit No. 172 of 2000 which was dismissed for default and the said Miscellaneous Case does not involve any substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution or any point of general public importance and, therefore, the High Court Division acted without jurisdiction and committed an error of law apparent on the face of record to allow the hearing of the said Miscellaneous Case by the High Court Division for restoration of the said Title Suit which was dismissed for default. He next submits that the Appellate Division erred in dismissing the case in the ends of justice and for the sake of complete justice, the appeal should have been allowed.

9. We have heard Mr. Abdus Salam Khan and perused the record.

10. It appears that the point raised by Mr. Abdus Salam Khan was well answered in our judgment. We therefore find no cogent reason to review the same.

11. Accordingly, the review petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1416 of 2004
lawyer:
Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
Respondents ------ Not represented.
parties:
Shahidul Hoq @ Md. Shahidul Hoq ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner & others Comilla ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 18th July, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4555 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J : This petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment dated 18.7.2004 of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4555 of 2002 making the Rule absolute which was obtained against the judgment and decree dated 15.1.2001 of the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1991 reversing those of dated 4.4.1991 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla in Title Suit No. 121 of 1990 decreeing the suit.

<u>2. The respondent instituted the above Title Suit No. 121 of 1990 praying for declaration   that the plaintiff i.e. the Government of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh, is the owner of the suit land and that the ex parte decree dated 4.3.1975 passed by the learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge), 1st Court, Comilla in Miscellaneous Case No. 104 of 1974 is collusive, fraudulent, null and void stating, inter alia, that Mr. Kazi Golam Mohiuddin Faruki (G.M. Faruki) was the original owner and possessor of the suit land along with other lands and Settlement Khatian No. 4 was prepared in the name of the Court of Wards on his behalf; G.M. Faruki was permanently residing in Comilla and his house was known as "Faruki House", after partition of India in 1947 G.M. Faruki left Comilla and was living at Calcutta permanently and he also died there leaving behind no issue; one Syed Md. Barek, the predecessor of defendant No.1, was staying in the said "Faruki House" with his family and G.M. Faruki did not transfer any property to the said Syed Md. Barek; according to the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 the entire property of the G.M. Faruki vested in the Government; some part of the suit land is used as local hat/bazar and some part of it is in the possession of the Government Tahsil Office and in Dag No. 564 there is a pond which is used by the staff of the Tahsil Office and also by the shopkeepers of local hat/bazar and the employees of respondent cultivations fishery in the said pond; the respondent had also been possessing some portion of the suit land by filing up the low land and thereby improving the hat/bazar; S.A. record was wrongly prepared in the name of G.M. Faruki instead of the respondent; thereafter one Mrs. Sahera Khatoon filed Miscellaneous Case No. 104 of 1974 praying for correction of the khatian and got exparte decree dated 4.3.1975 which clouded the title of the respondent in the suit land and hence the suit. The defendant petitioner contested the above suit by filing written statement contending that late Mr. Kazi Reaz Uddin Ahmed was the owner of the suit land and he died leaving his son Nawab Sir G.M. Faruki and 5 daughters namely (1) Raheta Khatun (2) Amena Khatoon (3) Fatema Khatoon (4) Halena Khatoon (5) Shahera Khatoon as his heirs; Rahela Khatoon died leaving her only one son Syed Md. Barek as her heir; Syed Md. Barek also died leaving his two sons Syed Abdur Rahim and Syed Md. Jafor Sadek as his heirs; thereafter the said Syed Abdur Rahim died without any issue and his share devolved upon Syed Md. Jafor Sadek and thus Syed Md. Jafor Sadek became the owner and possessor of the suit property; thereafter through amicable settlement the whole property was recorded in the name of Nawab Sir G.M. Faruki along with other co-sharers of the property; a miscellaneous case filed for correction of record of right by Sahera Khatoon in which the respondent was made a party and notice of the said case was duly served upon the respondent but the respondent not being present at the time of hearing of the case on 4.3.1975, an ex parte order was passed for correction of the record and thereafter the record was duly corrected; that Syed Md. Abdur Rahim paid rent for the suit land and got receipts (Dakhilas); after the death of Syed Md. Abdur Rahmi his brother Syed Md. Jafor Sadek because the sole owner of the suit land; on 20.1.1987 the said Syed Md. Jafor Sadek transferred the suit land to Md. Shahidul Hoq, the defendant No.2 petitioner, by a registered sale deed and thus the defendant No.2/ petitioner became the owner and possessor of the suit property and none else was/is in possession of the same on behalf of the respondent. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Comilla after hearing, decreed the suit. On appeal the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat after hearing, allowed the appeal, Then the respondent moved the High Court Division whereupon Rule was issued in Civil Revision No. 4555 of 2002 and the High Court Division after hearing made the Rule absolute.</u>

3. The learned counsel appearing for the defendant No. 2/ petitioner submitted that I the appellate court, the final court of facts, on consideration of the evidence and other materials on record allowed the appeal and the High Court Division failed to consider that the plaintiff respondent having failed to prove that the suit land is excess land of the landlord it cannot be said that the plaintiff respondent has right, title and interest in the suit land and as such the finding of the trial Court about the right and title of the plaintiff/respondent in the disputed land is not at all sustainable; the High Court Division also failed to consider that through amicable settlement, the suit land was recorded in the name of G.M. Faruki including other co-sharers of the property and that the respondent was made party to the Miscellaneous Case No. 104 of 1974 and notice was also served upon the respondent and the respondent not being present at the time of hearing of the case on 4.3.1975 an ex parte order was passed directing correction of the record of right and subsequently the records have been corrected.

<u>4. As it appears the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence on record found that the plaintiff/respondent claimed that the suit land along with other property belonged to G.M. Faruki and during the settlement survey the suit property was shown in the custody of Court of Wards; D.W.1 in his cross examination admitted that there is no document to show that the father of G.M. Faruki was the owner of the suit property; D.W.1 also admitted that the property was recorded under C.S. Khatian No. 34 of Debiddar Mouza in the name of court of Wards on behalf of G.M. Faruki which shows that G.M. Faruki was the owner and possessor of the suit property and there is nothing on record to show that any of the sisters of G.M. Faruki ever inherited the same from their father; D.W.1 also admitted in his cross-examination that the suit property was never transferred or gifted away to any one by G.M. Faruki and he also admitted that the plaintiff respondent has taken over the property of Faruki Estate and thus the exchange of property by a deed of Ewaz has no basis; the witness of the plaintiff respondent also categorically deposed that the disputed land was vested in the Government and since G.M. Faruki left the country the plaintiff respondent is possessing the same; the High Court Division further found that the trial court disbelieved the photocopy of the rent receipts as well as the claim of possession of the defendant petitioner in the suit land and the trial court also found that although the definite case of defendant petitioner was that notice in the miscellaneous case was duly served on the plaintiff respondent but he took no steps the service of notice on consideration of both oral and documentary evidence the trial court also found that the defendant petitioner had no title or possession in the suit property and that the exparte decree obtained on 4.3.75 in the miscellaneous case was obtained by fraud; the High Court Division further found that the judgment of the trial court is well reasoned and elaborate and is amply supported by evidence and the lower appellate court failed to reverse the findings of the trial court by cognate reason; the High Court Division in its judgment also referred to the case of Md. Afaz Uddin Mollah and others vs. Md. Maizuddin Shaikh reported in BCR 1983 (AD) 48 wherein it was held that reversal of the trial court judgment without adverting to the evidence on which the trial court's judgment is based is not a proper judgment of reversal.</u>

5. We are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of the evidence and the materials on record arrived at a correct decision and there is no cogent reason to interfere with the said decision.

6. The petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 717 of 2005
lawyer:
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-record ------ For the Petitioner.
Respondents ------ Not represented.
parties:
Md. Maniruddin ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Totab Ali @ Kutun Ali being dead his heirs: Mazeda Khatun and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated February 16, 2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2754 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Main J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment dated February 16, 2005 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2754 of 1997 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and order dated May 7, 1997 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 52 of 1994 allowing the same upon reversing the judgment and order dated April 13, 1994 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Gaffargaon, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Case (pre-emption) No. 29 of 1993 allowing the same. The Miscellaneous Case was filed under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act.

2. Facts in short, are that the preemptor sought to preempt the land transferred by the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed dated April 4, 1978 claiming to be the co-sharer of the holding by inheritance and by purchase and also claiming to be owner of the land contiguous to the land transferred by the deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz, stating that the pre-emptee i.e. opposite party No.1 (in the Miscellaneous Case) is a stranger and that the opposite party Nos. 2-6 (in the miscellaneous case) had transferred the land sought to be preempted by the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed beyond the knowledge of the preemptor, that the opposite party No.1 from his very childhood till attaining majority stayed in Wafejuddin's house as foster son of Wafejuddin and used to cultivate his land and also used to look after his land and as such preemptor had no knowledge about the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed by which land which is part of preemptor's homestead has been transferred, that on September 1, 1989 pre-emptor opposite party No.1 (in the Miscellaneous case) called a 'salish; to sell the land sought to be preempted and also the structures thereon as well as the pond and in that 'salish' opposite party No.1 (in the Miscellaneous case) disclosed abduct the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed dated April 4, 1978 and thereupon the pre-emptor obtained the certified copy of the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed and filed the Miscellaneous case within the period of limitation, 'that there is no legal bar in having the land pre-empted.

3. The case of the preemptee (opposite party No.1 in the Miscellaneous Case) in short, is that the land sought to be pre-empted is 1.14 acres and the same has been recorded in the name of Wafejuddin alias Afajuddin in ROR khatian No. 146, that land owned by the pre-emptor's predecessor has been listed in ROR khatian No. 148 and as such pre-emptor is not a co-sharer of the land of ROR khatian No. 146 that the preemptee is a stranger in ROR khatian No. 146, and that the pre-emptee has created a separate jama in  respect of his land: and mortgaged the same to the Agricultural Bank in 1982, that Heba-bil-Ewaz deed dated April 4, 1978 was created to the very knowledge of the preemptor and others and the possession of the land gifted was made over to the preemptee, that preemptee is owning and possessing the land of plot No. 322 by cultivating through the bargadar, that opposite party Nos. 2-6 are the heirs of the donor and they were aware of the Heba-bil-Exaz deed and that after the death of the donor when his heirs tried to create trouble there was a 'salish' and as per award of the 'salish' pre-emptee paid Tk. 1,000/- to the opposite party No. 3, that recently defendant Nos. 2 and 3 while disturbing pre-emptee the local Commissioner measured the land fixed the boundary, that the pre-emptor in collaboration with the opposite Nos. 2 and 3 violated the award of the 'salish', that pre-emptor and others had the knowledge about the deed from very beginning and as such contention of the pre-emptor knowing about the deed for the first time on September 1, 1989 is not correct and as such the Miscellaneous case is liable to be dismissed.

4. The opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 contested the Miscellaneous case by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that pre-emptee was the foster son of Wafejuddin, that because of difference of opinion between Wafejuddin on the one part and the wife and children on the second part he stayed in the house of preemptee and taking advantage thereof the pre-emptee by forging signature of Wafejuddin created the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed dated April 4, 1978, that opposite party Nos.2 and 3 came to know about the said Heba-bil-Ewaz deed on September 1, 1989 and became certain on September 3, 1989 upon obtaining certified copy, that as against the said deed these opposite parties filed 1 Suit No. 25 of 1990 in the Court of Assistant Judge but the same was dismissed and that the appeal being No. 106 of 1991 against the judgment and decree passed in Suit No. 25 of 1990 is pending and as such the Miscellaneous Case is liable to dismissed.

5. The trial Court allowed the prayer for pre-emption. On appeal the appellate Court set aside the judgment and order of the trial Court on the finding that the miscellaneous case is barred by limitation. The appellate Court while setting aside the judgment and order of the trial Court observed that heirs of Wafejuddin, i.e. the donor of the land to the opposite party No.1, in collusion with the pre-emptor has filed the Miscellaneous Case to deprive the pre-emptee of the land which he has got on the basis of  a genuine document, that pre-emptor failed to prove that he had the information of the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed on the date alleged for the first limo and that the date of knowledge claimed by the pre-emptor is a got up story, that pre-emptor and the opposite party Nos. 2-6 were very much aware about the transaction from its beginning and that only to take the Miscellaneous Case out of the clutch of limitation by making untrue statements the pre-emptor  has filed the Miscellaneous case.

6. As against the judgment of the appellate Court the pre-emptor moved the High Court Division. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record concurred with the finding of the lower appellate Court that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation and thereupon discharged the Rule.

<u>7. We have heard the learned Advocate on record and perused the materials on record. The undefined position, is that Miscellaneous Case was filed on 17.10.1989 seeking preemption of a transaction that took place on April 4, 1978 (the document was registered on August 8, 1978). The preemption was sought alleging that the preemptor came to know about the transfer for the first time on September 1, 1989 and thereafter he became certain about the transfer upon obtaining certified copy on September 12, 1989. It was alleged that the preemptee disclosed about the transfer for the first time in a 'salish' held on September 1, 1989 is seen from the judgment of the appellate Court that the preemptor to establish his case about the knowledge of the transaction did not depose in Court. Preemptor's son figured as P.W.1 in the Miscellaneous Case and it is seen form judgment of the appellate Court that said P.W.1 although deposed on behalf of his father but there is nothing on the record to show that in the 'salish' wherein disclosure about the transfer was said to have been made P.W.1 was present. No explanation was offered as to why the preemptor did not depose in the case. It is also seen from the materials on record that no reliable evidence was placed on record to substantiate the contention of the preemptor that he had no knowledge about the transfer before September 1, 1989. In the background of the said state of the matter the appellate Court reversed the judgment and order of the trial Court on the finding that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation. The Advocate-on-record failed to point out any misreading or non-consideration of evidence by the lower appellate Court was committed in arriving at the finding as to question of limitation. The High Court Division on Consideration of the materials on record concurred with the findings and decisions of the appellate Court. Since non-consideration or misreading of the evidence on the part of the appellate Court in arriving at the finding that the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation was pointed out and since there is no error in the judgment of the High Court Division of the kind calling for interference by this Division, we do not find any merit in the petition.</u>

<u>8. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.</u>

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 872 of 2008
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the petitioner 
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on Record ----- For the Respondent Nos. 1-3 
Respondent Nos. 4-6 ----- Not represented
parties:
Kazi Ali Ahmed ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Mohammad Nurunnabi and others ----- Respondent
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 05. 03.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Petition No. 1760 of 2006.)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J.:- This leave petition is arises out of judgment and order dated 5.3. 2008 passed in Civil Revision No. 1760 of 2006 of by the High Court Division affirming the judgment and decree dated 24.4.2006 passed in Title Appeal No. 173 of 2004 by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayanganj, reversing the judgment and decree dated 6.6.2004 passed in Title Suit No. 106 of 2001 by the Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayanganj. 

2. The respondent Nos. 1-3 hereof as plain-tiffs filed Title Suit No. 106 of 2001 in the court of Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayanganj, against the appellant hereof as defendant No. 1 and the respondent Nos. 4-6 hereof as defendant Nos. 2-4, praying for declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 is illegal, not valid, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending, amongst others that in the C.S. record the suit plot was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 392 in the name Chitu Mia (8 annas) Afsin Matbar (4 annas) and Babar All (4 annas), which they were owning and possessing as such and that the suit plot No. 752 consists of 27 decimals land, which on mutual partition said Afsin Matbar and Babar Ali have been possessing exclusively in open assertion of their right, title and interest therein and subsequently said suit plot of 27 decimals fell in the saham of Afsin Matbar on a subsequent mutual partition and while said Afsin Matbar was thus owning and possessing he died leaving behind two sons, four daughters and one wife, who inherited the property and were possessing and enjoying in ejmali and thereafter an amicable partition vide deed dated 12.11.1980 the suit land measuring 27 decimals fell in the saham of three daughters of Afsin Matbar and the husband and two sons of Kuti Bibi, another (laughter of Afsin Matbar (since deceased), and they were thus owning, possessing and enjoying the said property in ejmali and thereafter they sold out the suit land on different dates to plaintiff No. 1 (9 decimals), the defendant No. 2 (9 decimals) and defendant No. 3 (9 decimals), vide registered sale deeds and accordingly the plaintiffs mutated their names and were playing Government's rates and charges against receipt since their purchases in 1984 and that during S.A. survey operation the suit plot was wrongly recorded in the name of Sultan Mia and that the defendant No. 1, being son of Sultan Mia, taking advantage of said wrong recording in the S.A. Khatian, on 5.3.1999 tried to forcibly enter into the suit land but became unsuccessful being resisted by other plaintiffs' men and hence the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 55 of 1999 for permanent injunction against the defendant No. 1 and his son Kazi Masum in the court of Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj, which on contest was dismissed on the findings that earlier the defendant No. 1 got a decree in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 declaring his title on the suit land. 

3. The suit was filed challenging the wrong recording of the Khatian published in the name of Mosammat Daulat Bibi, Sukuri Bibi, Sonai Bibi and Rahela but the present plaintiffs were not made party therein and the suit was decreed ex-parte, inspire of the fact that Sukuri Bibi @ Kuti Bibi died in the year 1974, Daulat Bibi died in the year 1982 and Rahela died in the year 1984 and that Sonai Bibi was then 'residing at a different place, other then the address which was mentioned in the plaint of the Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 and thus on the basis of false report as to service of summons, the suit was made ready for hearing and was decreed ex-parte and that the cause of action for the instant suit arose when the Title Suit No. 55 of 1999 was dismissed on the ground of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998. The instant Title- Suit No. 106 of 2001 being dismissed on contest and being aggrieved there against the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 hereof preferred Title Appeal No. 173 of 2004 before the District Judge, Narayanganj, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayanganj, by the Judgment and decree dated 24.4.2006 allowing the appeal, setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Court below, and declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 was obtained fraudulently and illegal, not valid and not binding upon the plaintiff- appellants holding,  amongst others, that the suit was decreed against dead persons namely Sukuri Bibi, Rahela and Daulat Bibi, and being aggrieved there-against the defendant respondent No. 1 as petitioner preferred Civil Revision No. 1760 of 2006 in the High Court Division, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, and a Rule was issued thereon which has been disposed of by the impugned judgment and order dated 5.3.2008, discharging the Rule without any order as to costs, observing that the summons in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 were also not duly served. Now the said defendant No. 1 as appellant has come up with the instant leave petition. 

4. Perused the' leave petition as well as the judgments of the Court below and heard the learned Advocate. It appears though P.Ws. 1, 2, 3, and 5 have categorically stated about the dated of Kuti Bibi, Rahela and Daulat Bibi in the year 1984 and about the non-service of summons of Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 upon the said persons, who were defendants in the suit, the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the instant suit being Title Suit No. 106 of 2001, relying on the decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998. It appears that the Appellate Court below on due consideration of the evidences on record allowed the appeal holding that the suit as framed and filed is maintainable inasmuch as in the suit a prayer was made for declaring that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 9 of 1998 was illegal, fraudulent and not binding upon plaintiffs and therefore dismissing of the suit by the court below on the ground that "the possession and title of the plaintiffs were not proved" was not proper. The High Court Division in discharging the Rule has observed that the Appellate Court below carefully and clearly discussed the evidences on record and after proper assessment of the evidences on record came to its finding that the plaintiffs by producing the title deeds and Khatians as well as the oral evidences proved their case of title and possession and that in view of the settled principle of law that in exercising revisional power the finding of facts, whether concurrent or not, arrived at 'by the appellate court is final, unless it could be shown to be manifestly perverse. The High Court Division relying on the decision in the case of Khurshid Ali and others Vs. Noorjahan Bewa And others, reported in 15 BID (AD) 82, and in the case of Hazari Bala Sana and another Vs. Niron alias Niranjan Mandal and other, reported in 17 BLD (A1))295, wherein their lord-ships of the Appellate Division have held that finding of facts by the appellate court should not be disturbed unless those were found to be perverse and or there is non-consideration or misreading of the material evidences on record, which in the instant case has been found to be absent by the Revisional Court. The decision with observations given by the High Court Division appears to be in accordance with law and no interference is called for. 

5. Grounds set-forth in the leave petition appears to be of no substance in view of the observations made and the findings of the courts below. In the premises we do not find any merit in the application. 

6. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.  

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1368 of 2004
lawyer:
Abul Quasem, Advocate-on-Record. ----- For the Petitioner 
Respondents ----- Not represented
parties:
Most Jubeda Khatun ------ Petitioner.
VS
Md. Khuda Box & others ------ Respondents.
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 24.04.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4787 of 1997.)
full_judgment:
M.M. Ruhul Amin J: Delay of 04 days is condoned.

2. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.04.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4787 of 1997 discharging the Rule.

3. Short facts are that the plaintiffs instituted Partition Suit No. 29 of 1986 in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Ghatail, District-Tangail for partition of ejmali property. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 28.09.1989. Thereafter, the defendant-petitioners filed an application under Order IX Rule XIII of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside the ex-parte decree. On the ground that summons of the original suit was not served upon the defendant and the plaintiff managed a false report of the process server in respect of service of summons and by practicing fraud upon the Court obtained the ex-parte decree in question on 28.09.1989. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1989.

4. The plaintiff opposite parties entered appearance in the case and filed written objection stating, inter alia, that the summons upon the defendants was duly served by the process server in presence of Mukabela witnesses and as such the petitioner was aware institution of the suit and the date of ex-parte decree. Both the parties adduced evidence in the miscellaneous case and the trial court dismissed the case. On appeal, being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1994, the appellate court upon hearing also dismissed the miscellaneous appeal. Thereafter, the petitioner moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule.

5. We have heard Mr. Abul Quasem, the learned Advocate-on-Record for the petitioner and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers.

6. It is not disputed that the Partition Suit No. 29 of 1986 brought by the plaintiff-respondents in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Ghatail, District-Tangail was decreed ex-parte on 28.09.1989. It is also not disputed that Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1989 under Order IX Rule XIII of the Code of Civil Procedure was brought by defendant-petitioners on the ground of non-service of summons and the same was dismissed by the trial court on the ground of limitation and also on the ground that the defendant Petitioners failed to prove that non service of summons of the original partition suit as alleged by them.

<u>7. It is on record in the process server Afzal Hossain who was examined in the miscellaneous case, in his evidence stated that the summons of the original suit was duly served upon the defendant-petitioners. It further appears that P.W.1 son of defendant No.4 who deposed in the miscellaneous case in his evidence stated that summons of the original suit was duly served upon his father that is defendant No.4 of the suit. The trial court and the appellate court concurrently found that the petitioners had failed to prove that summons of the original suit was not served upon them and accordingly dismissed the case.</u>

8. The High Court Division after assigning cogent reasons affirmed the concurrent findings of the trial court and the appellate court and the present petitioner before the High Court Division could not show any misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence by the courts below.

9. In the circumstances, we do not find any cogent reason to interfere with the judgment of the High Court Division.

10. The leave petition is dismissed.

End.

lawyer:

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 24th day of February, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1632 of 2007).
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim CJ: This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 24th day of February, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.  1632 of 2007 discharging the Rule arising out of the order No. 3 dated 01.03.2007 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 371 of 2006 directing the petitioner to present the aforesaid revisional application brought against the order dated, 27.02.2006 passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka now 6th Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 allowing the application under Order VI rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the respondent No. 1 for amendment of plaint.

2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that on 17.03.2005 the respondent Nos.1-4 filed an application under Order VI rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint of Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 which was filed by their predecessor in 1984 stating, inter-alia that the defendant No. 1petitioner by filing a written statement in the said suit categorically claimed ownership of the suit property adverse to that plaintiffs-respondent Nos. 1-4. It is absolutely necessary for the plaintiffs to amend the plaint for final adjudication of the real question of ownership in the suit property. In the said petition for amendment the plaintiffs proposed that in the cause title page of the suit after the address of the defendant No. 3 the words and figure 'suit for ejectment of lessees. Suit valued at TK. 71,000.00 will be deleted and the following words and figure are to be inserted 'suit for declaration and for khas possession. Suit valued at TK. 60,00,000.00' and that in the prayer portion of the plaint the prayer No. (a) will be deleted and the following prayer shall be inserted that a decree be passed against the defendant No. 1 and in favour of the plaintiffs declaring that the plaintiffs are the sixteen annas owners of the 'B' scheduled property and that the proposed amendment for declaration of title is, merely an additional relief for necessary and appropriate relief and that the proposed amendment will not change the nature of the suit for eviction.

3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material allegations contending, inter-alia, that the defendant. No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 828 of 1979 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title which was converted into a suit for declaration of title and partition. The said suit is now pending before the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka at present 6th Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka wherein it is renumbered as Title Suit No. 290 of 2004. In the said suit the predecessor of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos.1-4 filed written statement on 19.03.1980 stating the plaintiff was the licensee of his mother in the suit land. Thereafter, in 1984 the predecessor of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos. 1-4 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 381 of 1984 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for ejectment of licensee against the defendant No. 1-petitioner which is now pending before the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka at present 6th Joint District Judge, Dhaka as Title Suit No. 218 of 2003. Both the suit has been continuing simultaneously, The defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 categorically claimed ownership over the suit property firstly in 1979 through Title Suit No. 290 of 2004 and thereafter in 1985 through the written statement filed by this petitioner as defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 and after about 26 years of the institution of Title Suit No. 290 of 2004 and after 21 years of the institution of the ejectment suit the present petition for amendment to the plaint of this suit praying turning this suit for ejectment of licensee into a suit for declaration of title and khas possession is barred by the law of Limitation. Since 1980 by filing written statement in Title Suit No. 290 of 2004 and since 1984 through Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 is the, licensee of the grandmother of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos.1-4 and as such, they are now estopped from raising new plea of title in accordance with the principle of law of estoppel. That from the proposed amendment petition it is clear that the plaintiffs have set up a Completely different and new case in their amendment petition. If this petition is allowed it will change the entire nature and character of the suit and the suit will convert into a suit of another new nature and character and in the name of amendment one should not he allowed to alter the fundamental character of the suit nor be allowed to turn his suit into a suit of new character and hence the petition for amendment is liable to be rejected.

4. Mr. Mohammad Ali Akanda, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division committed error of law in construing the judgment passed in Civil Revision No. 1701 of 2005 as reported in 58DLR211 and Civil Revision No. 2288 of  2006 in deciding the judgment passed Civil, Revision No. 1632 of 2007. The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division as well as the District Judge failed to consider that the amendment raising valuation at TK. 60,00,000.00 in place of TK. 71,000.00 and other matters having been subject matter of challenge in Civil Revision Petition under Section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the valuation of TK. 71,000.00 put by the plaintiff-respondents shall determine the jurisdiction of Court in respect of filing and moving Civil Revision Petition under Section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure and hence it is liable to be interfered with. The learned Advocate also submitted that the points of law involved in the matter are of great public importance.

<u>5. It appears that the opposite party instituted a suit showing valuation of TK. 71,000.00 and subsequently, by amendment raised the valuation to the time of TK. 60(sixty) lacs. It appears that the trial Court allowed other prayer of amendment. It appears that the defendants filed an application under Order XVII rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the trial Court and the trial Court while allowing the amendment rejected the said application by the said impugned order. The High Court Division in discussion of the jurisdiction of the District Judge considered that the District Judge has no pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain a revisional application in the instant case. It further appears that trial Court amended the plaint and raised the valuation. It is the plaintiff who is to determine the valuation in a suit. Whether the amendment is lawful or not is the subject matter of the revisional Court which could be determined in due course. It appears that the plaintiffs preferred an application for amendment and on contest the same was allowed and accordingly plaint was amended. Any action thereafter is to be based on the amendment plaint.</u>

6. In view of the above, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

7. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2469 of 2009
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioners.

VS

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 7.5 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3631 of 1994.)
full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J: By this petition, the petitioners challenged the judgment and order dated 7th May, 2009 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3631 of 1994.

<u>2. Short facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are that the Hossain Ali, Kanchan Bibi, Hason Bibi, Asia Begum, Abdul Gafur Hawlader, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner Nos. 1(a) to 5(d), Ahmed Ali Talukder, Abdul Aziz Talukder and Adam Ali Talukder (the plaintiffs) instituted Title Suit No. 77 of 1987 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jhalakati for declaration of title in respect of 1.38 acres out of 5.14 acres of land of S.A. Plot Nos. 591 and 593 of S.A. Khatian No. 311 and for further declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 is illegal, collusive and void. Their case, in short, is that Afaz Uddin, owned 5.14 acres of land who died leaving behind two sons and two daughters who inherited the same. Taking advantage of the plaintiffs minority during the last settlement operation, Jabed Ali, son of Rahman Ali in collusion with the settlement staff got the suit lands recorded in his name. Defendant Nos. 1-9 thereupon  instituted Title Suit No. 106 of 1986 in the Court of Munsiff, Jhalakati for declaration of title in respect of the lands in plot No. 591 of S.A. Khatian No. 311 and for recovery of possession. The defendant Nos. 2-5 having realised the defect filed a solenama on 8th September, 1986 admitting the plaintiffs' title of that suit. Kashem Ali and Sonai Bibi, son and wife of Rahman Ali thereupon instituted Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 for partition in First Court of Munsif, Barisal and obtained a decree on 22nd December, 1969 which was collusive. No summons of the said suit were served upon them and that they had no title in the suit lands. The said decree was forged and collusive, and the plaintiffs had no knowledge about the said decree. Respondent Nos. 1-3 also instituted Title Suit No. 34 of 1977 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Jhalakati for declaration of title in respect of 1.38 acres of land in the suit Khatian and for further declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 106 of 1986 is illegal, void and collusive. The defence case of respondents is the plaint case of Title Suit No. 34 of 1987.</u>

3. The learned Senior Assistant Judge took tip both the suits analogously and by judgment and order dated 19th September, 1990 dismissed Title Suit No. 34 of 1977 and decreed Title Suit No. 77 of 1987 in part declaring the decree passed in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 illegal, void and collusive. The respondents being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred Title Appeal Nos. 126 and 127 of 1990 respectively. The learned Subordinate Judge, First Court heard both the appeals analogously and by judgment and order dated 14th June, 1994 dismissed the appeals.

4. The respondents thereupon moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 3631 and 3633 of 1994. A Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment made the rule in Civil Revision No. 3631 of 1994 absolute and set aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 77 of 1987 and discharged the other rule.

<u>5. Admittedly the plaintiff No. 6 Abdul Gafur deposed as P.W3 in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 stating that his father Afazuddin was the original owner of the suit lands who gave some lands to his uncle Rahman Ali. This statement sufficiently proved that he had knowledge that Rahman Ali got some lands from his father and that he had also knowledge about the decree passed in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969. In view of the above, the claim of the plaintiffs that they had no knowledge about the decree passed in the said suit is baseless statement. The Courts below ignoring this admitted fact set aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.  138 of 1969. The Court of appeal below being the final Court of fact without at all considering the Material evidence and other materials on record maintained the decree on the reasoning’s that the respondents who are the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 34 of 1987 failed to prove their possession in respect of 1.38 acres of land, and abruptly came to the conclusion that since the respondents failed to prove their title in respect of /4/annas share in the suit lands, the decree passed in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 was not sustainable in law. This finding proved that the Court of appeal below maintained the decree on the weakness of the defendants cast, which is not a legal ground for passing a decree.</u>

6. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence on record particularly of the statements of Abdul Gafur, the plaintiff No. 6, made in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 rightly held that the plaintiffs had knowledge about the decree passed in Title Suit No. 138 of 1969 and that the suit having been filed after 18 years of passing the decree is hopelessly barred by limitation.

7. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the teamed Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners failed to repel the findings and observations arrived at by the learned Single Judge of High Court Division on the point of limitation. In view of the above, we find no merit in this petition.

8. The petition is accordingly dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1303 of 2004
lawyer:
Md. Nurul Amin, Advocate instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioners.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 20th April, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2020 of 1995)
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J : This petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment dated 20.4.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2020 of 1995 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated 3.9.1994 of the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), First Court, Bagerhat passed in Title Appeal No. 65 of 1986 affirming those of dated 28.1.1986 of the learned Assistant Judge, Bagerhat Sadar passed in Title Suit No. 106 of 1972 decreeing the suit.

2. Noor Mohammad Mallik, the predecessor of the respondents, instituted Title Suit No. 533 of 1968 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 106 of 1972 praying for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for perpetual injunction with alternative prayer for recovery of possession stating, inter alia, that the suit land, which belonged to Ramjan Sheikh in occupancy right, was auction purchased by Alep Hawlader in a rent sale; subsequently for arrears of rent the suit land was again put in auction when the plaintiff auction purchased the same on 15.6.1942 in Rent Execution Case No. 362 of 1942 in the benami of Atahar Ali Khan, the proforma defendant No.4; after the said sale was confirmed on 7.7.1942 the plaintiff took delivery of possession on 10.9.1942 through court; subsequently the plaintiff in Non-Judicial Miscellaneous Case No.46 of 1943 annulled all the encumbrances upon the suit land after due service of notice under section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act 1885; as the ex-tenants did not give up possession the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 106 of 1953 and got a decree and in execution of the said decree got possession through court; at that time the defendant No. 1-3, the heirs of Ramjan Sheikh, on arriving at a compromise, wanted to purchase the suit land from the plaintiff and accordingly the plaintiff, through his benamdar the proforma defendant No.4, by several registered kabalas sold some lands in favour of the above defendants on receipt of the entire consideration money which he spent for the education of his son Dr. Badiuzzaman Mallik MRCP; in course of time enmity cropped up between Atahar Ali Khan, the proforma defendant No.4 and Arshad Mallik, the second son of the plaintiff, relating to their business and then out of grudge and enmity the proforma defendant No.4 created the disputed kabala in favour of defendant Nos. 1-3 in respect of the suit land without the knowledge and consent of the plaintiff; the proforma defendant No.4 had no right, title or possession in the suit land but on the strength of the above kabalas the defendant Nos. 1-3 denying the title of the proforma plaintiff in the suit land threatened to dispossess him from the suit land and hence the suit. The defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation; the proforma defendant no. 4 is the real owner of the suit land and he was not the benamder of the plaintiff and the defendants acquired title to the suit land by their purchase from proforma defendant No.4; the defendant Nos. 1-3 being not in good terms with the brother of the plaintiff, the proforma defendant No. 4, at the instance of the plaintiff, got the custody of the title deed of the defendants and that the plaintiffs have no title or possession in the suit land. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing, decreed the suit. On appeal the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) dismissed the appeal. On revision the High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule.

3. The learned counsel for the defendant petitioner submitted that the High Court Division did not at all consider that the suit is barred under section 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the plaintiff could not prove even the specific year of dispossession not to speak of the specific date but even then the trial court decreed the suit; the High Court Division failed to consider that all the documents relating to the suit land including the kabalas executed by the proforma defendant No.4 in favour of the defendant Nos. 1-3 prove the ownership of the proforma defendant No.4 in the suit land and the plaintiff is thereby not permitted to deny this fact by oral evidence; the trial court as well as the appellate Court applied erroneous mode of appreciation of evidence in arriving at their conclusion as to the existence of benami transaction notwithstanding the fact that the plaintiff could not prove elements of benami transaction i.e. (a) motive of the transaction, (b) the dealing with the property and the (c) relationship between the parties; the proforma defendant No.4 executed 3 kabalas in the year 1958 in respect of the homestead of the defendants and 2 kabalas in the year 1959 in respect of the suit land against consideration; even if the proforma defendant No.4 is considered as ostensible owner even then the rights of the defendant Nos. 1-3 are protected by law; the S.A. record of right finally published in the year 1956 were prepared in the name of the defendants and the instant suit has been filed in the year 1968 and S.A. Record, being evidence of possession, the suit is also barred by limitation; since P.W.1 admitted his knowledge about the disputed kabala from the time of its execution he waived his right, if any, by acquiescence as he filed the suit long after 10 years; the trial court believed the evidence of P.Ws. merely because of the financial and social status of the plaintiff.

<u>4. As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that the original documents relating to auction purchase, confirmation of auction sale and delivery of possession of the auction sold property i.e. Exts. 3,4, 5A and 7 to 8(h) came from the custody of the plaintiff and the plaintiff also produced the documents relating to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 106 of 1953, and Ext.5, the certified copy of the above decree shows that the said suit was decreed and in pursuance of the said decree the plaintiff got delivery of possession of the suit land through court; both the courts below also concurrently found that the plaintiff successfully proved the auction purchase of the suit land in the banami of proforma defendant No.4 and that the trial court has clearly noticed that the proforma defendant No.4, being a mere benamder of the plaintiff did not contest the claim of the plaintiff; since the trial court as well as the appellate court considering the evidence on record came to the conclusion that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land at the time of the institution of the suit and during pendency of the suit he was dispossessed by the defendants the above finding can not be disturbed by the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction specially when the learned advocate for the petitioner could not point out any misreading of evidence or non-consideration of the materials on record by the courts below; the submission of the learned advocate of the petitioner that the suit was barred under auction 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no application in the facts and circumstances of the present case; the defendant Nos. 1-3 who allegedly purchased the suit land from proforma defendant No.4 also could not prove that the proforma defendant No.4 was in possession of the suit land when he sold the suit land to the defendant Nos. 1-3.</u>

5. We are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of the materials on record arrived at a correct decision and there is no cogent reason to interfere with the same.

6. The petition is dismissed.

End.
