case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 27.08.2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3727 of 2002)
full_judgment:
A. B. M. Khairul Haque J:- This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.8.2002, passed by a Single Judge of the High Court Division, in Civil Revision No. 3727 of 2002, discharging the Rule and affirming those dated 24.7.2002, passed by the District Judge, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 177 of 1977, and those dated 9.7.1977, passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka, in Miscellaneous Case No. 62 of 1995.

<u>2. The facts in short are that the appellant instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 261 of 1963 in the Third Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka, on 5.9.1968, praying for a decree for eviction of the defendant as licensee. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 27.2.1975 and thereafter Execution Case No. 14 of 1975 was filed. The defendant on 4.3.1975, instituted a miscellaneous. case being Miscellaneous Case No. 54 of 1975 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, praying for setting aside the aforesaid ex-parte decree and by an order dated 27.3.1975 the operation of the cx-parte decree was stayed but the appellant inspite of the aforesaid order of stay, evicted the defendant from the suit property. Thereafter, on the application of the defendant, the Court by its order dated 30.8.1980, directed the appellant to hand over possession of the suit property to the defendant within 24 hours.</u>

3. Being aggrieved, the appellant filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 400 of 1980 before the District Judge, Dhaka. After hearing, the said appeal was dismissed by a judgment and order dated 29.9.1980. Thereafter, a revisional application under section 115 of the Code was preferred by the appellant being Civil Revision No. 1321 of 1980. The High Court Division by its Judgment and order dated 26.2.1991, set aside the judgment and order dated 29.9.1980, passed by the appellate Court and directed the, learned Assistant Judge to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 54 of 1975, within one month from the date of receipt of the record. The said Miscellaneous case was allowed by the judgment and order dated 09.09.1991 and the ex-parte decree dated 27.2.1975 passed in Title Suit No. 261 of 1968 was set aside. Thereafter the defendants filed an application on 28.10.1991 under section 144 of the Code read with Section 151, praying for restitution of possession of the suit property. This petition was registered as a miscellaneous case being miscellaneous case No. 69 of 1991. This miscellaneous case was rejected by an order dated 19.11.1992 on the ground that the necessary documents were not furnished in support of the prayer for restitution.

4. Thereafter, a review petition was filed on 2.1.1993 being Review Miscellaneous Case No. 62 of 1995, contending inter alia that the papers and documents in support of the possession of the defendant had been filed earlier in Court.

5. The learned Assistant Judge also found the necessary documents in the record of the suit. Thereafter, by his judgment and order dated 9.7.1997, allowed the review miscellaneous case and directed restitution of possession of the suit property.

6. As such, the plaintiff filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 177 of 1977 before the District Judge, Dhaka. This was also dismissed by the Judgment and order dated 24.7.2002 with partial modification. Thereafter, the appellant filed a revisional application under section 115 of the Code before the High Court Division being Civil Revision No. 3727 of 2002.

7. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, on hearing found that the ex-parte decree of eviction was passed in respect of the suit premises. The suit premises as described in the plaint, comprised of schedules A, B, and C properties and consequently the defendant Md. Sekander Ali was evicted therefrom in execution of the decree and since the decree recorded in Title Suit No. 261 of 1968 stood set aside, the legal heirs of the deceased defendant are entitled to restitution of possession in respect of A, B and C schedule properties. Being aggrieved, by the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the plaintiff filed the instant appeal before this Division.

8. Leave was granted to consider, firstly, what was the suit property and whether the respondents are entitled to restitution of the properties mentioned in schedules A, B and C or only the property as mentioned in schedule -C in the plaint.

9. Mr. Rafique-ul Huq, the learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants submits that the property mentioned in schedule C to the plaint is the suit property and the decree was passed to evict the defendants from the said property alone. Accordingly, in pursuance of the Execution Case No. 14 of 1975, the defendant was evicted from the C schedule property only but not from either A or B schedule properties as mentioned in the plaint.

10. He further submits that the learned Judge in the High Court Division erred in law as well as in facts in not appreciating that the defendants were not evicted other than the suit property which is mentioned in schedule C to the plaint, as such, illegally directed restitution in respect of all the properties described in schedules A, B and C to the plaint.

11. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned senior counsel, appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondents, submits that the defendants were evicted from the properties mentioned in schedules A, B and C in pursuance of the ex parte decree and the subsequent execution case. He points out that the plaint, the decree and the petition for execution case, all those documents contained the above 3(three) properties. Besides, referring to the additional paper-book filed on behalf of the respondents, he submits, the warrant to the bailiff received by him on 22.8.1980, contained all those three properties and after execution by delivery, the plaintiff himself received the khas possession of all the properties mentioned in schedules A, B and C in the said warrant, by putting his signature on 23.8.1980, in presence of the witnesses. As such, he submits, all the Courts below rightly directed restoration in respect of all three properties.

12. We have heard the learned advocates of both the sides and perused the papers kept in the paper-books.

13. It appears that the plaintiff-petitioner filed a suit praying for eviction of the defendants from the suit premises. The plaint contains three schedules. The prayer made in the plaint are as follows:

a) a decree for eviction of the defendants in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants,

b) delivery of vacant possession of the suit land and the suit but thereon in favour of the plaintiff after removing all obstacles and obstructions therefrom;

(c) ------------------

(d) -----------------

14. The prayers do not specify the suit land but the plaint contains three schedules. Besides the decree the petition for execution the warrant to the bailiff all contain the three schedules. As such, apparently it would appear that the prayer for decree for eviction would be in respect of all three properties mentioned in the schedules A, B and C.

15. But from the plain reading of paragraph 8 and 9 of the plaint it would appear that the plaintiff has his building in the schedules A and B properties and the defendants are admittedly living in schedule C property. The relevant portion of paragraph 8 and 9 of the plaint reads as follows:

"8. ------------- the plaintiff again brought the defendants back and allowed them to live as licensee in another but standing on the 'C' schedule land hereinafter called the suit property.

9. -------------- The defendants had to live in a rented house outside the A and B schedule land as stated in paragraph no.8 above."

16. The above averments made in the plaint show that the purpose of the suit was to evict the defendants from the C schedule property alone.

17. In due course, the decree was passed to evict the defendants from the suit property. As such, it would be presumed that the decree was passed in respect of the C schedule property alone.

<u>18. It appears that the plaint contains all three schedules. The A schedule mentions C.S. Plot nos. 18 and 19 while the B schedule mentions C.S. Plot no. 17 and nothing much, but the C schedule describes the concerned property on the north-western corner of 'A' schedule of C.S. Plot no. 19 4 with the S.A. and R.S. plot members. Besides, the Municipal holding number has also been given with the description of the huts and structures thereon.</u>

19. As such, it appears that the 'C' schedule property is the suit property.

<u>20. It is true that the plaintiff wrote in the back of the warrant to the bailiff that he received the possession of the properties mentioned in Schedules A, B and C but 110 this mere endorsement cannot alter the fact that the suit property is only to the extent of property mentioned in Schedule C to the plaint.</u>

21. Under such circumstances, the respondents are entitled to restoration of C schedule property only.

22. There is, however, no legal impediment to recover the properties, in accordance with law, if the defendants were earlier dispossessed, in excess of the property mentioned in Schedule C to the plaint.

23. With this modification of the Order passed by the High Court Division in its Judgment and Order dated 27.8.2002 passed in Civil Revision No. 3727 of 2003, this appeal is disposed of without any order as to cost.

24. The concerned Senior Assistant Judge is directed to restore possession of the property mentioned in schedule C to the plaint in favour of the defendants within the period of 1 (one) month from the date of receipt of this Order.

End.

Md. Abdul Matin J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 08.05.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3149 of 1998 reversing the judgment and decree dated 28.05.1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No. 264 of 1995 reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.09.1995 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge of Mongla Thana in Title Suit No. 80 of 1994.

2. The facts, in short, are that the respondent No. 1 instituted Tide Suit No. 80 of 1994 on 29.11.1994 before the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla within the District Bagerhat for declaration of title in kha schedule land against the present petitioners.

3. The disputed land and other khas lands measuring 38. 12 acres and the under raiyates of C. S. Khatian No. 223 and possessed the same jointly and then Monohar Dakua died leaving no wife, sons and daughters and accordingly his share was devolved upon the other two brothers namely the plaintiff and proforma defendant No. 8 Kamal Dakua and the plaintiff from his own share transferred 2. 30 acres of land to others and retained 4. 05 acres and possessed the same jointly with other co-sharers and the plaintiff constructed houses and possessed the same and the plaintiff paid rents to the ex-land lords and possessed the same openly and adversely for more than 30 years.

<u>6. S. after settling rents in the names of Shetal Mondal, Katmai chandra Dakua plaintiff Ananda Chandra bakua and the defendant No. 7 Kalicharan Bairagee and delivered possession to them and thereafter again the rents of the aforesaid two plots fell dote and the landlords filed rent suit No. 75/ -53/ 76/ 53 and 77/ 53 against Shitol Mondal, Kamal Chandra Dakua, plaintiff Ananda Chandra and Kalicharan Bairagee and the aforesaid four tenants amicably settled the claims of the land lords and the aforesaid four tenants right and tile upon the C. S. plot No. 381 and 382 were confirmed and then the plaintiff and his brother Kamal Chandra Dakua on 19.06.1954 with the help of registered patta No. 831 made settlement of land measuring 2. 64 of plot No. 381 in favour of Sushil father of the defendant No. 2 and 3 and at that time the plaintiff Anandra Dakua as member of the joint family executed and registered the aforesaid patta No. 831 dated 19.06.1954 and delivered possession to the aforesaid tenants and the names of the aforesaid tenants Sushil, the father of the defendant No. 2 and 3, pulin Bihari defendant No. 1, Malati Bala the defendant No. 4 were not recorded in the S. A. Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 before the Revenue department and opened the S. A. Khatian as S. A Khatian No. 229/1 and the C. S. Plot No. 381 and S. A. Plot No. 680 measuring 5.10 acres of which 3.77 acres were wrongly recorded in other khatians and the plaintiff Ananda, the aforsaid kalicharan and Sarola the wife of Shetal file title Suit No. 523 of 1957 before the 2nd Munsif Court, Bagerhat it and the suit was decreed and they cm reeled their names by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 1165 under Section 54 of the State Acquisition an Tenancy Act, 1950 and the plaintiff him self from the disputed land sold 19 acres of land on 27.08.1974 with the help of registered sale deed No. 1839 in favour of the defendant No. 1 and 4 i. e. Pulin Bihari Bairagee and kalicharan Bairagee and after the death of Sushil his share was inherited by his two sons the defendant No. 2 and 3 i.e. Narayan Mondal sold .44 acres of land from the disputed plot along with other lands on 24.06.1989 with the help of registered sale deed No. 834 in favour of the defendant No. 6 Taif all and the defendant No.4 Maloti Bala sold . 88 acres of land on 07.04.1993 with the help of registered sale deed No. 534 to Abel kazi and Yanunj kazi the sons of defendant No. 6 and after taking settlement and purchasing land by the defendant No. 1 pulin Bihari Bairagee and kalicharan Bairagee the papers were with the custody of the landlords Nag and Menus and the plaintiff himself admitted the same in Title Suit No. 523 of 1957 and the plaintiff never challenged the patta dated 19.06.1954 within twelve years from the date of attaining majority in the year of 1957 and the plaintiff instituted a false suit which was liable to be dismissed with cost.</u>

10. It appears that the trial court on proper assessment of evidence decreed the suit. But the appellate court without averting to those finding set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and dismissed the suit.

12. In such view of the matter we find no substance in this petition which is accordingly dismissed.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 2.7.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 415 of 2003.)
full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J: Petitioners are the heirs of defendant in a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land, preferred this petition for leave to appeal from the judgment of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.415 of 2003 reversing those of the learned Subordinate Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.503 of 1999.

2. One Brajabashi is the admitted owner of the suit land. Plaintiffs are claiming title in the suit land on the strength of registered deeds from Abdur Rashid, Mamtaz Begum and others who got the same from Shahida Begum. Said Shahida Begum claimed to have purchased the suit land by registered deed dated 4th July, 1974 from Asrafuddin, who also claimed to have purchased from Brajabashi. The defendants, on the other hand, claimed to have purchased the suit land by registered deed dated 8th January, 1979 from Shahida Begum. Therefore, both the parties admitted that by purchase Shahida Begum was the owner of the suit land.

3. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record held that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title, possession and dispossession in the suit land and accordingly dismissed the suit. The High Court Division, however, found the plaintiffs; title and decreed the suit on the reasoning’s that the plaintiffs acquired title on the strength of exhibit-3 series and on the other hand, the defendant failed to produce title deed in support of his case and that he filed a photostat copy of a deed which was not also exhibited in the suit. On the question of possession, the High Court Division assessed the evidence on record and found that though the defendant claimed possession on and from 8th January, 1979, the plaintiffs having instituted the suit on 29th November, 1989 within the period of limitation, the suit is not barred by limitation.

4. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that since the suit is for possession followed by dispossession, the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit without any finding of plaintiffs possession followed by dispossession.

5. We have perused the judgments and other materials on record. The findings of the High Court Division on the point of plaintiffs acquisition of title in the suit land are based upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record and in this regard Mr. Mahbubey Alam finds it difficult to repel any of the findings arrived at by the High Court Division. Admittedly Shahida Begum was the owner of the suit land from whom the defendants are claiming title. The defendants did not file their basic document by which they are claiming title to the suit land. They even did not give any explanation in that regard. On the other hand, the plaintiffs filed their title deeds and the High Court Division on perusal of the same was satisfied that the plaintiffs had acquired title in the suit land. We find no illegality in the judgment of the High Court Division in finding the plaintiffs title in the suit kind.

<u>6. Now the question is whether the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree for recovery of khas possession in view of the fact that the High Court Division has not arrived at any definite finding as to when they have been dispossessed by the defendant. Since the defendant did not file documentary evidence in support of his title, even if his claim of taking possession of the suit land on 8th January, 1979 is taken to be true, the suit having been instituted within a period of 12 years from that date, the plaintiffs have acquired better title than the defendant. The High Court Division, in the premises, is perfectly justified in decreeing the suit. We find no merit in the contention of Mr. Mahbubey Alam.</u>

7. The petition is accordingly dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal is against the judgment dated January 13, 2004 of a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 744 of 1997 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated July 6, 1996 of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Comilla, in Title Appeal No. 76 of 1994 dismissing the same and there-by affirming the judgment and decree dated February 28, 1994 of the Court of Assistant judge, Nangalkot, Comilla in Title Suit No. 24 of 1991 decreeing the same. The suit was filed seeking declaration that the judgment and order dated June 29, 1987 passed in Miscellaneous Case (pre-emption) No. 6 of 1984 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Nangalkot was fraudulent and as such liable to be set aside.

2. It was the case of the plaintiffs that certain Elahi Baksha had interest to the extent of 8 annas 6 gondas and 2 karas in the property described in the schedule 1 by inheritance from his mother and Elahi Baksha died leaving 2 daughters, by name, Syedennessa and Jobeda Khatun and 2 sons, Hasanuzzaman and Joynal Abedin and a widow by name Khatijan Bibi who died leaving 2 sons, defendant No.1 and another and 2 daughters, that Hasanuzzaman died leaving 3 sons and 3 daughters, that defendant No.10, daughter of Ellahi Baksha transferred the schedule land to her co-sharer defendant No.9 and he is possessing the same, that defendant No. 9 transferred 26 decimals of land from the land of schedule No.1 to defendant No. 69 by the kabala dated March 4, 1984 and also transferred 12 decimals of land from the land of schedule No. 1 by the kabala of the same date to the plaintiffs, that plaintiffs and the defendant No. 69 purchased 38 decimals of land and developed the same by earth filling and constructed homestead and are possessing the same. Defendant No. 1, now deceased, was aware of the purchase, development and possession of the land, that defendant No. 9 is a co-sharer by inheritance. Defendant No. 1 since deceased (survived by defendant Nos. 2-8) filed Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1984 under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act on February 26, 1984. Defendant No.9, vendor of the plaintiffs, contested the said case. The Miscellaneous Case was allowed on June 29, 1987 and as against that defendant No. 9 filed Appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 88 of 1987 but the defendant No. 9 withdrew the same on being influenced by the defendant Nos.2-8, that the plaintiffs after having had knowledge about the judgment of the Miscellaneous Case filed the suit seeking the relief as stated hereinbefore.

<u>3. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-8 by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint. It was the case of the defendants that the suit so filed was barred by limitation and the suit as framed is not maintainable. It was also the case of the defendants that the kabalas on the basis of which defendant No.96 is claiming the land are ante-dated kabalas and the same have been brought into existence during the pendency of the pre-emption case, that defendant No.9 who contested the case did not disclose about the transfer to the plaintiffs, that plaintiffs were not necessary parties in the pre-emption case, that no fraud was committed in obtaining the order in the Miscellaneous case and that the judgment and order passed in the Miscellaneous case is quite legal.</u>

<u>4. The trial Court decreed the suit on the finding that the plaintiffs have been able to establish their case and the suit is quite maintainable and the same is not barred by limitation. The trial Court also held that the plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit and they have their homestead in the land in suit, that defendants failed to dislodge the evidence of P.W. 2 who have deposed that the plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit.</u>

5. It may be mentioned the Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1984 was filed on February 26, 1984 to pre-empt the transfer that took place on February 20, 1982 and the prayer for pre-emption was allowed on June 29,1987.

6. The suit was filed stating that the plaintiffs came to know about the order of pre-emption initially on December 8, 1990 and that become definite about the order allowing the Miscellaneous Case on obtaining certified copy on February 5, 1991. The plaintiffs claim is based on Ext.1 i.e. the kabala executed on November 7, 1983 and registered on March 4, 1984 and also based on Ext. 2 i.e. a kabala executed on February 14, 1984 and registered on March 4, 1984.

7. The defendant went on appeal. The appellate Court dismissed the appeal on the finding that from the evidence on record it is seen that the plaintiffs and defendant No. 9 have title in the land of item No. 1 of schedule 1 and they are in possessing of the said land and that order of pre-emtion was obtained in Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1984 without impleading the plaintiffs and the defendant No. 69 and as such the order of pre-emption so obtained is fraudulent and liable to be set aside and that if the same is not set aside the plaintiffs and the defendant No. 69 would be prejudiced, that the suit is not barred by limitation and as such plaintiffs are entitled to the relief sought in the suit and the suit as framed is quite maintainable.

8. The defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division in the facts of the case, particularly because of the Exts. 1 and 2 on the basis of which the plaintiffs and the defendant No. 69 claimed title, held that plaintiffs and defendant No.69 were not necessary parties in the Miscellaneous Case and as such order obtained in the Miscellaneous Case without impleading the plaintiffs and the defendant No. 69 can not be said to have been obtained fraudulently. The High Court Division also held that plaintiffs and defendant No. 69's vendor contested the Miscellaneous case and he lost in the same and that although he filed appeal but ultimately withdrew the same. The High Court Division finally held that the courts below in misconstruction of the document Exts.1 and 2 decreed the suit on the finding that plaintiffs were necessary parties in the miscellaneous Case and that order of the Miscellaneous Case as was obtained without impleading the plain-tiffs the same was fraudulent.

9. We have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and perused the materials on record. The Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1984 (filed on February 26, 1984) was filed seeking pre-emption of the transfer for pre-emption was allowed by the order dated June 29, 1987. The plaintiffs are claiming title in the land of item No.1 of schedule 1 on the basis of their purchase by Exts.1 and 2. It is seen from the materials on record that Ext.1 was executed on November 7, 1983 and was registered on March 4, 1984 and that Ext. 2 was executed on February 14, 1984 and the same was registered on March 4, 1984. It is evident that he transfer sought to be pre-empted in Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1984 took place at a time when the plaintiffs did not acquire any interest in the land of the holding. In that view of the matter we are of the view High Court Division was not in error in dismissing the suit. The learned Counsel for the petitioner although argued that on the registration of the document on March 4,1984 title of the plaintiffs in view of the provision of section 47 of the Registration Act become perfect on and from the date of the documents so executed and in the instant case execution of the Exts.1 and 2 being prior to the filling of the Miscellaneous case, the plaintiffs were very much necessary party in the Miscellaneous Case. The contention so made is not legally well conceived since in the Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1984 pre-emption was sought in respect of the transfer that took place on February 20, 1982 and as such the pre-emptor was required to implead in the Miscellaneous Case those who were the co-sharers on February 20, 1982 and not the person who have acquired interest in the land of the holding sub-sequent to the transfer sought to be pre-empted and as such the High Court Division has quite correctly held that the plaintiffs were not necessary parties in the Miscellaneous Case and consequent thereupon order of pre-emption obtained therein without impleading the plaintiffs was not a fraudulent one.

10. In the light of the discussions made hereinbefore we find no substance in the petition.

11. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment dated 4.4.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 1001 of 1998 which arose out of judgment and decree dated 19.11.1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Rajbari allowing Title Appeal No. 21 of 1998 setting aside those of dated 31.1.1996 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gualundo, Rajbari in Title Suit No.9 of 1992 dismissing the suit.

<u>2. The respondents, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 895 of 1985 before the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Rajbari of declaration of title, for khas possession and also for further declaration that the compromise decree passed in Title Suit No. 220 of 1981 is collusive, void, illegal and not binding upon them on the averments that the suit land originally belonged to Shahiduddin Mollah who died leaving behind wife Sonai Bibi and minor son Sekandar Ali, Sonai Bibi sold the suit land to Nurun Nahar, predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered sale deed dated 17.11.1943; after the death of Nurun Nahar, her husband Asmat Ali Mollah and daughter, plaintiff No. 7, inherited the suit land as her heirs; after the death of Asmat Ali the plaintiff nos. 1-7 have been possessing the suit land as heirs; during his life time, Asmat Ali permitted Mofizuddin, father of the defendant Nos. 2-3, to live in the suit land and after the death of Mofizuddin, the plaintiffs asked defendant Nos. 2-3 to vacate the suit land but defendant Nos. 2 and 3 fraudulently inducted the defendant No. 1 in the suit land who by erecting 2(two) sheds and by denying the title of the plaintiffs started living in the suit land; thereafter the plaintiff came to know that the suit and has been wrongly recorded in the name of one Abdul Gani who has/had no title or possession over the suit land and hence the suit. The defendants, the petitioners herein, contested the above suit by filing written statement contending that the suit land originally belonged to Mahabuddin and others and one Shahiduddin possessed the lands with their permission; thereafter the name of Shahiduddin has been recorded in the P.S. Khatian No. 223 as a resident occupant tenant; Shahiduddin had no tenancy right in the suit land so after has death, his wife Sonai Bibi and son Sekandar got no right to the suit land; Mahtabuddin sold out 1.55 acres of land including the suit land to defendant Nos.1 and 2, who are brothers, by a registered deed of sale dated 19.1.44; thereafter the suit land was put into auction for arrears rent in Rent Suit No. 192 of 1946 and Abdul Gani Sardar, a relation of defendant No.1, purchased the suit land then he inducted the defendant No.1 into possession of the suit land as a bargader; the suit land has been rightly recorded in the name of Abdul Gani Sardar in S.A. Khatian; Mafizuddin the father of defendant No.2-3 was permitted to live in the suit land by Abdul Gani Sardar; after the death of Mofizuddin Abdul Gani Sarder sold the suit land to defendant No.1 by a Registered kabala dated 29.1.76 and after his purchase the defendant No.1 asked the defendant Nos. 2-3 to vacate the suit land and on their refusal filed Title Suit No. 220 of 1981 of khas possession; the above suit was decreed on compromise against the defendant Nos. 2-3; since then defendant No.1, by mutating his name, was living in the suit land with his family.</u>

<u>3. The learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge) Rajbari Sadar, dismissed the suit on 28.2.87. The plaintiffs then preferred Title Appeal No. 81 of 1987 and the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Rajbari who heard the appeal by judgment and decree dated 18.09.91 allowed the appeal and remanded the suit for trial afresh and on remand the above suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 9 of 1992. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing dismissed the suit holding that the suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff did not seek any relief against Exhibit-D, the Kabala dated 29.10.1996 executed by Abdul Goni in favour of defendant No.1. The plaintiff, being aggrieved filed Title Appeal No. 21 of 1986 before the learned District Judge, Rajbari. During pendency of the above appeal the plaintiff by filing an application prayed amendment of the plaint by way of including the relief that Ext-D is void and illegal and the appellate court allowed the amendment as prayed for. The learned Additional District Judge, who heard the appeal, found that Ext. D has been obtained by practicing fraud and allowed the appeal. On revision the High Court Division found that in Exbt-A the name of the executant of the deed were inforpolated (interpolated) and there is no explanation for such interpolation and there was also interpolation in Dag Nos. 594/595 by way of over writing with no explanation as to the over writings and further, in Ext. A, 25 decimals of land from Dag No. 202 was inserted later on; in Exhibit-B the signature of the then Munsif appeared to have been made on 15.04.47 but on the left side of the same Exhibit it has been written as 3774 of 1946; the courts below observed this execution case as doubtful; the report of the Advocate Commissioner showed that the structure erected by the defendants in the suit land were of recent time which believes the defendants case that they are on the suit land from the time of Akin Ali Mollah; the evidence on record show that deed of sale dated 17.11.43 was executed in favour of Nurun Nessa the predecessor of the plaintiffs.</u>

4. We have heard the learned Advocate-on-record appearing for the petitioner and also perused the materials on record. The learned Advocate-on-record could not point out any misreading and/or non-consideration of the materials on record and/or any error in the judgment of the High Court Division calling for interfere by this Division.

5. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 11.07.2010 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 134 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 11.07.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.134 of 2004 reversing the judgment and decree dated 22.03.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Gazipur, in Title Suit No. 42 of 1991 dismissing the Suit.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, arc. that the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.42 of 1991 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Gazipur impleading respondent Nos.l-5 as the defendants praying for declaration that the order dated 28.03.1989 passed by defendant No. 1, Additional - Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, cancelling the permanent settlement of the plaintiffs was illegal, void, collusive and without jurisdiction. The plaintiffs also prayed that they have sixteen annas right and title and interest in the suit land and for further declaration that the title of the plaintiffs has not been extinguished by the deed dated 24.12.1990 executed and registered by defendant Nos. 4 and 5 in favour of defendant Nos. 6 in respect of the suit land, and that the said deed is illegal, void, without consideration and not acted upon.

3. The case of the plaintiffs-appellants, in brief, is that while in possession of the `Ka' schedule land as landless peasants, the plaintiffs 02.09.1986, 10.01.1987 and 09.01.1987 filed applications before the Government for getting permanent settlement of the suit land upon which Nathi No. 97/86-87, 179/86-87 and 180/86-87 were opened and approved. On 02.05.1987, 11.05.1987 and 10.05.1987 the deeds of settlement were executed and registered in favour of plaintiff Nos. 1-3 who have been in possession thereof on payment of rents to the Government. With the sole object of grabbing the suit land, defendant Nos. 4 and 5 have created some false and forged documents and managed to show them as the affected persons of L.A. Case No.71/1964-1965. The plaintiffs have paid rent and obtained rent receipts. On 15.08.1988, defendant No.4 confined plaintiff No. 1 in his office situated in Dhaka and took his signatures on some blank stamp papers following which the plaintiff No. 1 made a General Diary to that effect. Title Suit No. 1257 of 1985 instituted by defendant No. 7, Nurul Islam in the same Court claiming his title in the suit property as settlement holder is still pending. However, Title Suit No. 478 of 1981 instituted by Nurul Islam was dismissed. On 15.02.1991, defendant No. 6 took initiative to dispossess plaintiff Nos. 1-3 from the suit property claiming that they purchased the suit property but because of timely intervention of the plaintiffs, the defendants failed to dispossess them. The plaintiffs are illiterate and not aware of the notice published in the newspaper inviting objection from the claimants of the suit property. Defendant No. 4 managed to issue a collusive order dated 23.11.1988 not to deliver possession of the suit property in favour of plaintiffs and ultimately cancelled the settlement of the plaintiffs. Consequently, the plaintiffs were compelled to institute the suit.

4. Defendant Nos. 1-3, 7 and 4-5 filed 3 separate written statements in the suit. The case of the defendant Nos. 1-3 is that 43 acres of land of suit C.S. Plot No.39 were acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.71/1964-1965 for Roads and Highways Department and possession thereof was delivered to the Railway Department. Of the total acquired 43 acres of land, 19.94 acres were derequisitioned on 10.04.1980 and the possession thereof was delivered in favour of defendant Nos. 4 and 5 as affected owners of the suit property. The said property is not the khas land of the Government and when it came to the notice of the authority that 5.94 acres of land were settled in favour of plaintiffs as landless people, their settlements were cancelled and proposal was made to grant settlement from other khas land. The proposal for settlement in favour of plaintiffs is under process. The authority rightly cancelled the settlement of the plaintiffs and passed order not to deliver physical possession of the suit property to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs have not acquired any right to and title in the suit land. The Government did not have the right to grant settlement of the private land in favour of the landless people as khas land. The plaintiffs are not entitled to any relief in the suit.

5. The case of the defendant No.7 is that neither defendant Nos. 4 and 5 nor their predecessor Yasin Haji had no land in the suit plot. The R.S. record of the suit land is wrong and the plaintiffs have no right and title in the suit land. The suit land originally belonged to Kalishangkar Ray who transferred 2.03 acres of land to Dhakkhina Ranjan Ray for a consideration of Tk.98 by an unregistered deed of transfer. Md. Azman Ali, father of this defendant, purchased some land of C.S. Khatian No.18 of No Nos. 39 and 46 by the deed dated 21.05.1967 from Sushil Kumar Basu son of late Dakkhina Ranjan Ray. The aforesaid Md. Azam Ali took settle of 3.17 acres of land from plot No. 39 and .62 acre of land from plot No. 46 of C.S. Khatian No.67 on 17th Chaitra, 1337 B.S. While owning and possessing 6.92 acres of land by way of settlement and purchase Aram Ali died during the minority of defendant No.7 leaving him as his heir and successor. The draft S.A and R.S khatians were prepared in the name of his father but final S.A. and R.S. Khatians were wrongly prepared in the name of Government. As such, he instituted Title Suit No.470 of 1981 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Gazipur and, was renumbered as Title Suit No. 1257 of 1985. Again the suit was transferred to the First Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur and renumbered as Title Suit No. 302 of 1992.; Again on transfer the suit was registered as Title Suit No.99 of 1994 and has been pending for disposal. Neither the plaintiffs nor the other defendants have any right, title and interest in the suit land and as such, the plaintiffs are not entitled to any relief.

6. The case of defendant Nos.4 and 5 is that according to S.A. Khatian the suit land belonged to Hazi Yeasin, Zahuruddin, Zamiruddin, Miazuddin and others. In 1965 the Government had acquired 43 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 39 by L.A. Case No.71. Zahuruddin transferred 3.36 acres of land to his sons Saheb Ali and others by a deed of sale dated 04.01.1947. Saheb Ali and others transferred the same to one Ratan Petra by a registered deed of sale dated 17.06.1974. Subsequently, Ratan Petra transferred the same to defendant No. 5 by a deed of sale dated 17.03.1980. Bellla and others, sons of Yeasin Haji, had been in possession of the land of S.A. Khatian No.33. They transferred 3.72 acres of land to Tapan Chowdhury by a registered deed dated 01.07.1974 and they also transferred 3.72 acres of land to Swapan Chowdhury on the same date. Tapan Chowdhury and Shapan Chowdhury transferred 3.61 acres of land each to defendant No.4 by registered deeds dated 19.03.1980 and 17.03.1980 respectively. On 15.02.1980, Zamiruddin transferred .33 acre of land to Soheli who transferred the same to defendant No.4 by a registered deed dated 04.03.1980. Zamiruddin transferred .66 acre of land to Ehsan and Sultan Ahmed by the deed dated 15.02.1980 and Ehsan and Sultan Ahmed also transferred their purchased land to defendant No.4 by registered deed dated 14.03.1980. Abdul Gani, son of Zamiruddin, and Sahera Khanam wife of Hazrat Ali transferred some land to Nilufer Begum who transferred .18 acre of land to defendant No.5 by the deed dated 20.03.1980. Abdul Gani sold .44 acre of land to Mostafa Kamal by registered deed dated 15.02.1980 and Mostafa Kamal subsequently transferred the same to defendant No.5 by a registered deed dated 14.03.1980. Surjaban, wife of Raisuddin, sold .66 acre of land to Abdul Matin by a registered deed dated 05.02.1980 and Zamiruddin also sold .66 acre of land to Abdul Matin. After that, Abdul Matin sold .14 acre of land to defendant No.5 by a registered deed dated 26.04.1980 and delivered possession thereof. Kafiluddin and Aminul Haque transferred 1.92 acres of land to Sirajuddin on 15.01.1980 and Aminul Haque and Sirajuddin transferred 3.84 acres of land to defendant No.4 by a deed dated 12:03.1980 from suit plot No.39. Miazuddin and Malekjan transferred 2.16 acres of land of plot No.39 to Sarafat Ali alias Nur Mohammad Khan by a deed of sale dated 05.02.1980 and Malekjan sold 2.16 acres of land to defendant No. 5 by the deed dated 05.02.1980. While defendant Nos.4 and 5 were in possession of their purchased land of C.S. Plot No.39, the authority by memo dated 21.03.1980 directed to de-requisition the furnished land of the suit plot No.39 to handover to the original owners. Defendant Nos.4 and 5 were asked by the notice dated 14.06.1982 to return the money which they received as compensation from the authority. Defendant Nos. 4 and 5 mutated their names and 5.94 acres of land were settled in favour of plaintiffs but possession thereof was not delivered to them. The proposal for settlement was rightly cancelled. Defendant Nos. 4 and 5 returned the entire compensation money on 01.09.1980 and accordingly, possession of 19.84 acres of land was delivered to them on 28.04.1981. Defendant Nos.4 and 5 have been in possession of 16 annas land from before and they have acquired valid right and title in the said land. The suit land is not the khas land of the Government and as such the settlements of the plaintiffs were rightly cancelled. Meanwhile, the proposal has been made for granting settlement of different lands in favour of plaintiffs. The suit is false and the same is liable to be dismissed.

7. Defendant No.6 on 14.08.1997 appeared in the suit by filing vokalatnama and prayed for time to file written objection. Defendant No. 6 took adjournment unto 25.03.1998 for filing written statements but ultimately did not the any written statement in the suit. However, defendant No.6 fled an application under Order VII Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint. After hearing the parties the trial Court by Order No.121 dated 25.08.1999 rejected the application for rejection of the plaint. Since then defendant No.6 did not appear in the suit. The hearing of the appeal was concluded on 03.06.2010 and 06.06.2010 and was fixed for judgment. On that date defendant No.6 filed an application for accepting written statement and also filed a separate written statement in support of its case.

8. The trial Court dismissed the suit by the judgment and order dated 22.03.2004. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs filed First Appeal No. 134 of 2004. The High Court Division allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and decreed the suit by the judgment and order dated 11.07.2010.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 11.07.2010 passed by the High Court Division, defendant No.6-petitioner filed this leave petition.

10. Mr. M.A. Samad, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the Government initially cancelled the allotment of landless allottees by making decision to give them alternative khas land without canceling their registered deeds which the Government can do under Rule 103 of the Manual of 1987 and against such decision of the Government, one is under the legal obligation to file appeal before the concerned Divisional Commissioner, if aggrieved and as such the suit and the appeal filed by them are all premature because no cause of action arose as yet to file a declaratory suit I le further submits that the plaintiffs could neither prove their title nor possession in the suit land and that without reversing findings, on those issues of the trial Court, the high Court Division decreed the suit. He also submits that the plaintiffs staled to have taken possession of the suit land before registration of the deeds of lease and that the High Court Division failed to consider that nobody could take possession of khas land without registration of the deed of lease.

11. Mr. Khair Azaz Masud, learned, Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 1-3 and Mr. Zainul Abedin learned Advocate-on-Record on behalf of respondent No. 10 support the impugned judgment and decree delivered by the High Court Division.

12. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the impugned judgment and decree and the materials on record.

13. The high Court Division came to a finding that the plaintiffs could prove their title in respect of 5.94 acres of land by different deeds of lease which were proved before the Court in accordance with law. Having considered the evidence of the witnesses the High Court Division found that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their possession in the suit land prior to giving them delivery of possession of the suit land pursuant to different deeds of lease. The High Court Division noticed the trial Court considered the evidence of P.Ws. 1 and 3 and found that the trial Court misquoted their evidence relating to construction of boundary wall in the suit land by defendant No.6.

<u>14. Defendant No. 6, the main contesting defendant, however, did not file any written statement controverting the statements made in the plaint in the trial Court Defendant No.6, however, filed a written statement on the date of pronouncement of the judgment by the High Court Division. Filing of such written statement in the High Court Division in the First Appeal on the date of pronouncement of judgment is misconceived.</u>

15. The High Court Division found that the suit land was not vague and indefinite and as such it altered the finding of the trial Court which came to a finding that the suit land was vague and indefinite. The High Court Division noted that though defendant Nos.4 and 5 contested the suit in the trial Court, they did not appear before the High Court Division to contest the appeal and that there was no evidence before High Court Division to hold that defendant Nos.4 and 5 transferred the suit land to defendant No.6.

<u>16. It is contended by the petitioner that the suit is premature as the plaintiffs could have preferred an appeal before the concerned Divisional Commissioner against the cancellation of lease which was done by issuing a letter and not by any registered instrument. Such contention does not hold well on the ground that before taking any unilateral action against anybody he must be given an opportunity of being heard but no such opportunity was given to the plaintiffs. In addition, the plaintiffs not only filed the suit for declaration against the order of cancellation of lease but also for declaration of title to the suit land and for further declaration that the deed executed by defendant Nos. 4 and 5 in favour of defendant No. 6 is not binding on them. The appeal as stated by the petitioner could not give all the reliefs prayed for by the plaintiffs in the plaint of the suit. In such a situation, the door of civil Court is open to an aggrieved party. The jurisdiction of civil court cannot be ousted so lightly.</u>

17. The findings arrived at and the decisions made by the High Court Division having been made on proper appreciation of law and fact de not call for interference.

18. Accordingly, the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 28.10.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4069 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: The instant leave petition under Article 103 of the Constitution arises out of the judgment and order dated 28.10.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4069 of 2004 discharging the Rule, Which arose out of the judgment and order dated 3.6.2004 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat, allowing the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 38 of 1999 setting aside the judgment and order dated 30.05.1999 passed by the Assistant Judge, Rampal, Bagerhat, dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1998 tiled for restoration of Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 after setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 7.5.1997.

2. The plaintiffs are the petitioners before us.

3. The plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 for declaration of title and recovery of possession and on the date (7.5.1997) fixed for ex-parte hearing of the suit, the defendants of the suit did not appear, and accordingly the suit was heard ex-parte and being proved decreed. Thereafter, on 22.01.1998 the defendant Nos. 24 and 25 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1998 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 after setting aside the ex-parte decree passed on 7.5.1997.

4. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record and submissions of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties dismissed the case and being aggrieved there against the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 38 and 1999 was preferred before the District Judge, Bagerhat, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat, who allowed the appeal vide judgment and order dated 3.6.2004, there by allowed the miscellaneous case and restored the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 7.5.1997.

5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4069 of 2004, upon which the Rule was issued and thereafter the Rule was heard and disposed of by the High Court Division discharging the Rule against which the instant leave petition has been Preferred.

6. We have heard the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners and the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, and perused the application.

7. It appears that the Title Suit No. 103 of 4989 was decreed ex-parte on 7.5.1997 and the defendant-petitioners of the miscellaneous case contested the suit by filing written statement and they claim to have no knowledge about the ex-parte decree tilt 12.09.1998, on which date the said defendant-petitioners having come to Court to file written statement in Title Suit No. 111 of 1997 enquired about the fate of the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 and came to know about the ex-parte disposal of the Title Suit 103 of 1989. But while giving deposition in the miscellaneous case the P.W.1 on behalf of the petitioners categorically stated that."I have no other suit in the civil Court  except this suit. I am none of the T.S. No. 111 of 1997. I did not file hajira in T.S. No. 111 of 1997". He further deposed to effect that "no date was fixed for any step on 12.1.98 in T.S. No. 111 of 1997".

<u>8. The trial Court, on discussion on the aforesaid statements made in the application for restoration and the statements made while deposing before the Court, observed that the miscellaneous case has been filed with false statements and accordingly arrived at it's decision that the miscellaneous case is barred by limitation and the cause of action as stated in the plaint of the miscellaneous case is not correct.</u>

9. It appears that in disposing of the appeal the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat, observed that the defendant-appellants were interested in the suit for which they have filed the written statement in Title Suit No. 103 of 1989. But due to political rivalry they remained in custody for a long time and hence could not pursue their case in Court and the same was treated as sufficient cause. Further the Appellate Court relying on the provisions of Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure allowed the appeal awarding compensation costs.

10. The High Court Division accepted the reasons given by the Appellate Court below in allowing the miscellaneous appeal and observed that no illegality has been committed by the Appellate Court below in allowing the defendant opposite party to contest the suit on payment of the compensatory costs of Tk. 1,500/-.

11. The learned Advocate-on-Record appearing before for us submitted that both the Appellate Court below and the High Court Division erred in not considering the reasons given by the trial Court in dismissing the miscellaneous case inasmuch as there is no discussion on the caused of action disclosed in the application for restoration i.e. the miscellaneous case, in particular the case so far relate to the knowledge about the date of the ex-parte decree and the statements made before the Court while deposing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners and thereby arrived at an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice.

<u>12. The High Court Division further erred in not making any discussion and or arriving at any findings on the point of limitation, whereas the miscellaneous case has been dismissed on the point of limitation and that the High Court Division also misread the provisions of Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure inasmuch as restoration may be allowed under the said provisions awarding costs, if the case is filed within limitation.</u>

13. The learned Advocate-on-Record of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 supported the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division.

14. Considering the facts and circumstances the case and in view of the discussions made above, we find merit in the leave petition.

15. Accordingly, leave is granted to consider the Ground Nos. I, III and IV set forth in the leave petition, which are as under:-

"I. For that the High Court Division has failed to consider that the appellate Court below is wrong to find that the Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1998 preferred by the defendant Nos. 24 and 25 as petitioners from the judgment and order of ex-parte decree dated 07.05.1997 in Title Suit No. 103 of 1989, is barred by limitation as the date of knowledge of the petitioner on 12.01.1998 is totally false;

II. For that the High Court Division has failed to consider that the trail Court after properly considering oral and documentary evidence on record both oral and documentary rightly dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No.3 of 1998 of the defendant (present respondent Nos. 1 and 2) but the Court of appeal below without properly considering the same and without reversing the findings of the trial Court committed error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal and allowing, the said miscellaneous case of the defendant (present, respondent Nos. 1 and 2);

III. For that the P.W. 1 Sheikh Motahar Hossain in his examination deposition stated that while on 12.01.1998 he came to the Court for filing written statement in another Title Suit. No. 111 of 1997 he came to learn about the fact of ex-parte decretal of Title Suit No. 103 of 1989, but in his cross-examination he has stated that he had no bother suit except said Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 and that he is neither a tadbirkar of the said another Title Suit No. 111 of 1997 nor date of the said case was fixed on 12.01.1998 in the miscellaneous petition he stated that he had learnt of the disputed ex-parte decree of Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 on 12.01.1998 but the Court of appeal below without considering the same committed an error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal and allowing the miscellaneous case."

16. Security of Tk. 1000/- is to be deposited within 1 (one) month.

17. The petitioners are permitted to prepare the paper book out of Court in accordance with Rules.

18. Let the operation of the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division dated 28.10.2008 in Civil Revision No. 4069 of 2002 be stayed till disposal of the appeal.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2265 of 2011

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 25th of May, 2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1243 of 2008)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J.:- This civil petition for leave to appeal is, directed against the judgment and order dated 25.05.2011 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1243 of 2008 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are as follows:

<u>3. The predecessor of petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 141 of 1972 before the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Satkania, Chittagong against the predecessor of the defendants respondents for partition with declaration that the auction sale in Rent Execution Case No. 937 of 1944 is illegal, not acted upon and the defendant Nos. 1-6, 14-25 have no right and title.</u>

<u>4. The plaintiffs' case is that the property in schedule 1 and 2 belonged to Bacha Mia, Karam Ali, Abdul Ali, Ahmed Ali, Keramat Ali and Abdur Rahman. The property in Schedule 3 belonged to Abdur Rahman alone. The C.S. and R.S. khatian has been prepared accordingly. Abdur Rahman died leaving son Kabir Ahmed and daughter Hazera Khatun Bacha Mia died leaving brother Karam Ali as his sole heir. Abdul Ali died leaving brother Bacha and Karam Ali. Kabir Ahmed sold 5 panda land to Md. Suleman in 3 plots, but possession was given in one plot. Suleman sold to Faizur Rahman. Defendant Nos. 7-13, being heirs of Faizur Rahman, are possessing the sold land Karam Ali died leaving his sister Umeda Khatun who sold her entire share of the suit property to the plaintiffs by executing 3 kabalas and delivered possession to them and thus the plaintiffs own and have been possessing 5 kanis, 3 ganda and 3 kara and the defendant Nos. 7-13 own and have been possessing 10 ganda land in the suit property. The other defendants have no title, interest or possession in the suit property. Defendant No. 1 Abdul Khaleque is the son of Torafuddin who is the ex-landlord: the defendant No. 2 is his wife. Plaintiff Nos. 1-5 filed Other Suit No. 33 of 68 for injunction and got decree. They filed Other Suit No. 141 of 69 and got decree. The plaintiffs came to know about rent .decree and auction sale in Rent Execution Case No. 937 of 1944 only when Mosharraf Ali filed documents in Other Suit No. 33 of 68. The auction sale in Rent Execution Case No. 937 of 1944 and the decrees are all void and inoperative on account of non-service of summons and notices upon the parties and thus the plaintiffs prayed for declaration that the rent decree is void and the defendant Nos. 1-6 and 14-25 have no title in the suit property and also prayed for partition of the suit property.</u>

5. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaintiffs contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, and since the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit property as such their suit for partition on payment of fixed court fees is not maintainable. The schedule land was auction purchased by Shaham Ali in revenue sale and his grandfather took over lease of 2 kani, 7 ganda, 1 kara and 1 kranti land by registered patta. Defendant No. 4 son of defendant No. 1 purchased 1 kani land from the gradual heirs of C.S. tenant Latu and he is in possession. Defendant No. 1 purchased 14 ganda land from Karam Ali who got the same as heirs of Abdul Ali and Bacha Miah. He also purchased 3 ganda land from Asma Khatun who got the land from her husband Ahmed Ali. Thus the defendant No. 1 got 4 kani, 4 panda, 1 kara and 3 kranti land in schedule-1 properties. The documents submitted by the plaintiffs are all forged and fraudulent in respect of schedule-1 suit properties. The schedule-2 suit property was purchased by Mosharaf Ali in rent execution case who sold the same to the defendant No. 1 by registered kabala. The land in schedule 3 belonged to Abdur Rahman who sold 5 ganda land to defendant No. 1 in the benami of his sister's husband Faizur Rahman. Thereafter the said Abdur Rahman died leaving his son Kabir Ahmed who inherited the remaining 5 ganda land in schedule-3 and the defendant No. 1 also purchased the said 5 ganda land from Kabir in the benami of his cousin Sultan.

6. Defendant No. 4 in his written statement also denied all the material allegations of the plaintiffs and claim contended inter alia that he purchased 40 decimals of land by registered kabala from the heir of Latu as schedule-1 and prayed for separate saham.

7. Defendant Nos. 7-13 filed a separate written statement claiming that they own and have been possessing 2 kani, 13 ganda, 2 kara land in the suit property. Their predecessor Faizur Rahman purchased land from Suleman @ Kabir Ahmed by kabala dated 01.02.1985. Kabir Ahmed also sold 12 ganda and 3 kara land by kabala dated 12.07.1966 to Faizur Rahman Defendant Nos. 7-13 are in possession of the land. The plaintiffs' documents are false and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

8. Upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence and. materials on record the learned Senior Munsif by his judgment and decree dated 09.12.1974 decreed the suit with cost against the contesting defendants and ex-parte against the rest and allowed the plaintiffs to get a share of 5 kani, 3 ganda, 3 kara and the defendant Nos. 7-13 only 10 ganda share in the suit property. The rent decree and auction sale in question were declared void.

9. Against the said judgment and decree the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 preferred Other Appeal No. 30 of 75 in the Court of District Judge, Chittagong which was subsequently transmitted to the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong who upon hearing, dismissed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 09.01.2008 against the respondent No. 1 (predecessor of the present petitioners) and ex-parte against the rest without cost.

10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District judge, the defendants as petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 1243 of 2008 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule.

11. By the impugned judgment and decree the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree dated 09.01.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court Chittagong in Other Appeal No. 30 of 1975 and judgment and decree dated 09.12.1974 passed by the learned Senior Munsif, Second Court, Satkania in Title Suit No. 141 of 1972.

12. The plaintiffs as petitioners are now before us having filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal.

<u>13. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division most unfortunately failed to consider that the instant suit is a suit for partition and declaration. Admittedly title in the schedule 1 and 3 property has not been denied by the defendants in the suit, rather it was admitted. Dispute arose only regarding schedule 2 property. In that view of the matter, the suit for partition is well maintainable in law and the plaintiffs arc legally entitled to get saham at least from schedule 1 and 3 property. Accordingly, both the Courts below decreed the suit for partition giving saham to the plaintiffs and the defendants but the High Court Division without considering this aspect of the case, most erroneously upon misconception of law and misreading the evidence on record set aside the concurrent judgments of the Courts below traveling beyond the facts in the pleadings and as such the judgment and decree of the High Court Division is liable to he set aside. The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division failed to find that the trial Court as well as the Appellate Court in unequivocal terms found on evidence on record that the alleged auction was in respect of superior interest having right to collect rent and not in respect of the raiyati right and also found that the defendants could not produce any documents showing delivery of possession in the alleged auction case and could not prove their possession by oral evidence, which proves that the alleged auction was not acted upon. Moreover the alleged auction purchaser Mosharaf Hossain was not examined in the suit to prove the auction, and in the absence of any contrary evidence the concurrent findings of the Courts below cannot be reversed and disbelieved, but the High Court Division in its own motion made out a third case that the defendants filed document of possession which is contrary to the evidence on record, facts and circumstances of the case and as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division misread the facts of the case and evidence on record and erroneously found that the plaintiffs though they claimed that they filed Other Suit No. 41 of 1968 and Miscellaneous Case. No. 33 of 68 and got decree, but did not file any paper. The suits were in fact Other Suit No. 141 of 1969 and Other Suit No. 33 of 68 duly exhibited and also failed to find that the trial Court in its judgment directed the plaintiffs to pay deficit court fee of Tk. 40 for two declarations and failed to observe that deficit court fees can be paid at any time and for this reason only the suit could not have been dismissed.</u>

14. Mr. Golam Arshed learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division.

15. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned and perused the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

16. We find merit in the submissions, of the learned Advocate for the petitioners.

17. Accordingly, leave is granted.

18. Security of Tk. 1000/- is to be deposited within 1 (one) month.

19. The petitioner is permitted to prepare the paper book out of court in accordance with Rules.

20. Parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of possession and position of the suit land till disposal of the appeal.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 28th May, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil RevisionNo.3180 of 2000)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J.: Delay of 297 (two hundred ninety seven) days in filing the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is condoned.

2. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 28.05.2009 passed  by a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3180 of 2000 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated  31.05.2000 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Gazipur in Miscellaneous Case No.40 of 1998 allowing the application under order IX Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the opposite parties setting aside the judgment and decree dated 21.06.1998 passed by Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.97 of 1995.

<u>3. The relevant facts of the case are that the plaintiffs, respondents herein instituted the Title Suit No.97 of 1995 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), First Court, Gazipur impleading the petitioners as defendants for declaration of title to the suit land and also for declaration that Heba bil Ewaj Deed Nos. 6196 and 6197 dated 08.10.1976 are forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs.</u>

4. The opposite parties as defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint.

5. Upon hearing, the trial Court decreed the suit on contest by judgment and decree dated 21.06.1998. Then on 21.10.1998 the defendants as petitioners filed Misc. Case No.40 of 1998 under Order IX Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.97 of 1995. The trial Court allowed the said application by judgment and order dated 31.05.2000.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 31.05.2000 passed by the trial Court, the plaintiffs-opposite parties as petitioners filed Civil Revision No.3180 of 2000 under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court Division and obtained Rule.

7. By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree dated 21.06.1998 passed by the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.97 of 1995 and dismissed the miscellaneous case. Hence, the petitioners have filed the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Division.

8. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Munsur Habib, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 -8.

<u>9. It appears from the impugned judgment that the High Court Division noted on perusal of the records that the suit was decreed on contest on 21.06.1998 and thereafter on 21.10.1998 the defendants filed an application under order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground of non-service of summons. The High Court Division held that the provisions of order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure are not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case as the suit was decreed on contest and, therefore, the revisional application was not maintainable and hence the Rule was discharged. The High Court Division further observed that defendants had remedy by way of filing an appeal under Order XLI of the Code.</u>

10. When faced with the aforementioned facts and circumstances, Mr. Mahbubey Alam found it difficult to continue with his submission.

11. We do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and accordingly, the petition is dismissed. The petitioners are at liberty to take any appropriate steps in accordance with law.

End.

Abul Kalam Chowdhury, Advocate Instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 13th June, 2012 passed by the High Court. Division in Civil Revision No. 1065 and 1066 of 2011)
full_judgment:
Abdul Wahhab Miah, J. This 2(two) Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal are from the common judgment and order dated the 13th day of June, 2012 passed by a Division Bench of the high Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 1065 and 1066 of 2011 making the Rules absolute.

<u>2. Short facts essential for disposal of these petition are that the petitioner as preemptor filed Miscellaneous Case No. 14 of 1996 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Noakhali under Section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act or in the alternative under section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, for preemption of the case land. The preemptor at the same time also filed a suit being Title Suit No. 67 in the same Court for declaration that the so called ewaj Deed No. 15836 dated 28.11.1995 was an out and out sale deed.</u>

<u>3. It appears that the miscellaneous case and the suit were heard analogously and the learned Assistant judge by a common judgment and order dated 18.04.1999 rejected the miscellaneous case and also dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree passed in the suit the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 35 of 1999 and against the order passed in the miscellaneous case, the preemptor filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 21 of 1999 before the District Judge, Noakhali. The learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Noakhali on hearing the appeals together by a common judgment allowed the preemption application and decreed the suit. Against the said judgment and order and the decree of the Appellate Court passed in the miscellaneous appeal and in the title appeal respectively, the preemptee and defendant filed Civil Revision Nos. 1065 of 2011 and 1066 of 2011 respectively before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court by the impugned judgment and order made the Rules absolute, set aside the judgment and decree passed in the title appeal as well as the judgment and order passed in the miscellaneous appeal and sent the suit and the miscellaneous case back to the trial Court for fresh trial after framing proper issues in both the matter. "The High Court Division further directed the trial Court to hear the suit and the miscellaneous case simultaneously".</u>

<u>4. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division did not enter into the merit of the suit as well as the miscellaneous case and did not decide the issues involved therein. It took objection to the analogous hearing of the suit and he miscellaneous case, the nature of the suit and the miscellaneous case being different. However, it appears that the High Court Division made general observation as to when the exchange deed assumed the character of sale deed. It also observed that the property in the suit was a town property, as such, it had to be decided first whether "it is pre-emtable under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act or under section 24 of the Non agricultural Tenancy Act." but did not decide the question with reference to the evidence on record though the entire records were before it; hence these petitions for leave to appeal.</u>

<u>5. From the record it does not appear that any objection was taken by any of the parties at any point of time either before the trial Court or before the Appellate Court or even before the High Court Division as to the analogous hearing of the miscellaneous case and the suit. But the learned Judges in suomotu took the said objection and sent the suit and the case back to the trial Court for hearing afresh with direction to hear them simultaneously.</u>

<u>6. In view of the above, we find no other alternative, but to send the revisions back to the High Court Division for hearing afresh and dispose those in accordance with law on the evidence on record. Accordingly, these petitions are disposed of in the following terms:</u>

<u>7. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside. The Revisions are sent back to the High Court Division for hearing afresh and dispose them in accordance with law on the evidence on record.</u>

Let the revisions be heard and disposed of by the Bench presided over by Borhanuddin, J. expeditiously.

End.
